name: Old Fashioned
description: A classic template highlighting fine whiskey accented by aromatic bitters and rich demerara sweetness.
instructions:
1. Add bourbon, demerara syrup, and bitters to a mixing glass filled with ice.
2. Stir thoroughly for 25-30 seconds until well-chilled and properly diluted.
3. Strain into a rocks glass over a single large ice cube.
4. Express orange peel oils over the rim and garnish.

name: Negroni
description: An iconic Italian aperitivo balancing crisp botanical gin, bitter gentian and orange from Campari, and rich sweet vermouth.
instructions:
1. Combine gin, Campari, and sweet vermouth in a mixing glass with cracked ice.
2. Stir for 20-30 seconds until cold.
3. Strain into a chilled rocks glass over a large ice sphere or cube.
4. Garnish with a freshly expressed orange peel.

name: Boulevardier
description: A whiskey riff on the classic Negroni, created by Erskine Gwynne in 1920s Paris.
instructions:
1. Combine bourbon, Campari, and sweet vermouth in a mixing glass filled with ice.
2. Stir for 25-30 seconds until well-chilled and integrated.
3. Strain into a rocks glass over a large ice cube or into a chilled coupe.
4. Express orange peel oils over the drink and garnish.

name: Daiquiri
description: The quintessential Cuban sour balancing light rum, tart fresh lime juice, and sweet cane syrup.
instructions:
1. Add white rum, fresh lime juice, and cane sugar syrup to a cocktail shaker filled with ice.
2. Shake hard for 10-15 seconds until well-chilled and frosty.
3. Fine-strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Float a fresh lime wheel on top.

name: Manhattan
description: A foundational whiskey classic pairing spicy rye with herbal sweet vermouth and aromatic bitters.
instructions:
1. Combine rye whiskey, sweet vermouth, and Angostura bitters in an ice-filled mixing glass.
2. Stir smoothly for 30 seconds to achieve silky dilution and chill.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Garnish with a brandied cocktail cherry.

name: Margarita
description: A crisp Mexican tequila sour highlighting bright agave balanced by orange liqueur and fresh lime.
instructions:
1. Rub a lime wedge along half the rim of a coupe and dip into kosher salt.
2. Add blanco tequila, Cointreau, fresh lime juice, and agave nectar into an ice-filled shaker.
3. Shake vigorously for 12-15 seconds until frosty.
4. Fine-strain into the prepared coupe and garnish with a lime wedge.

name: Sazerac
description: New Orleans' official cocktail marrying robust rye whiskey with herbal Peychaud's bitters and an absinthe rinse.
instructions:
1. Chill a rocks glass with crushed ice, discard the ice, and rinse the glass with absinthe.
2. In a mixing glass filled with ice, stir rye whiskey, rich simple syrup, and bitters until cold.
3. Strain neat into the absinthe-rinsed glass.
4. Express lemon peel oils over the surface and discard the peel.
source: Antoine Peychaud & Leon Lamothe, New Orleans (c. 1850s)

name: Last Word
description: An equal-parts prohibition icon pairing botanical gin, herbal Green Chartreuse, bittersweet maraschino, and fresh lime.
instructions:
1. Combine gin, Green Chartreuse, maraschino liqueur, and fresh lime juice in an ice-filled shaker.
2. Shake hard for 12-15 seconds until thoroughly chilled.
3. Fine-strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Garnish with a brandied cherry.

name: Whiskey Sour
description: A benchmark sour featuring bourbon whiskey balanced against tart lemon juice and simple syrup.
instructions:
1. Add bourbon, fresh lemon juice, simple syrup, and a dash of bitters into an ice-filled shaker.
2. Shake hard for 12-15 seconds until properly chilled and diluted.
3. Double strain into a chilled coupe glass.
4. Garnish with Angostura bitters drops and a lemon wheel.

name: Gin & Tonic
description: The timeless British highball balancing aromatic botanical gin with bittersweet effervescent tonic and lime.
instructions:
1. Fill a highball glass with clear ice spears or cubes.
2. Pour in London dry gin.
3. Top gently with chilled tonic water.
4. Stir once gently to blend without losing carbonation, then garnish with a fresh lime wedge.

name: Dry Martini
description: The archetypal cocktail balancing crisp London dry gin with dry French vermouth and a dash of orange bitters.
instructions:
1. Combine gin, dry vermouth, and orange bitters in a mixing glass filled with cracked ice.
2. Stir briskly for 30 seconds until ice-cold and properly diluted.
3. Strain into a chilled martini glass.
4. Express lemon peel oils over the surface or garnish with an olive.

name: Mai Tai
garnish: Spent lime shell & fresh mint bouquet
description: Trader Vic’s legendary 1944 tropical drink balancing aged rum, nutty almond orgeat, fresh lime, and orange curaçao.
instructions:
1. Combine aged rum, fresh lime juice, orange curaçao, orgeat, and demerara syrup in a shaker with crushed ice.
2. Shake vigorously for 10-12 seconds until frosty.
3. Pour unstrained into a double rocks glass.
4. Garnish with a spent lime half and fresh mint sprig to evoke an island with a palm tree.

name: Cosmopolitan
description: The defining modern classic popularized by Toby Cecchini, balancing citrus vodka with tart cranberry, lime, and orange liqueur.
instructions:
1. Add citron vodka, Cointreau, fresh lime juice, and cranberry juice to an ice-filled shaker.
2. Shake vigorously for 12-15 seconds until thoroughly chilled.
3. Fine strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Express and flame an orange peel over the surface and drop into the drink.

name: Espresso Martini
description: Dick Bradsell’s 1980s London sensation uniting rich espresso, vodka, coffee liqueur, and velvety crema foam.
instructions:
1. Add vodka, coffee liqueur, fresh hot espresso, and simple syrup into a shaker with hard ice.
2. Shake hard and fast for 15 seconds to build a dense, creamy foam head.
3. Double strain promptly into a chilled coupe glass.
4. Float three coffee beans on the crema in a triangle for health, wealth, and happiness.

name: French 75
description: Named after the rapid-firing French 75mm field gun, pairing bright gin sour acidity with effervescent sparkling wine.
instructions:
1. Add gin, lemon juice, and simple syrup to an ice-filled shaker.
2. Shake briefly for 10 seconds until chilled.
3. Strain into a chilled flute or coupe glass.
4. Top gently with cold sparkling wine and garnish with a long lemon twist.

name: Aperol Spritz
description: Venice’s ubiquitous sunlit aperitivo following the classic 3-2-1 ratio of prosecco, bitter aperitivo, and soda.
instructions:
1. Fill a stemmed wine glass with abundant fresh ice.
2. Pour in sparkling wine followed by Aperol in an equal or 3:2 ratio.
3. Add a splash of club soda and gently stir once from the bottom up.
4. Garnish with a fresh orange slice.

name: Sidecar
description: The definitive brandy sour created in World War I Paris, balancing rich oak and fruit of Cognac with dry orange liqueur and lemon.
instructions:
1. Optionally coat half the rim of a chilled coupe with superfine sugar.
2. Add Cognac, Cointreau, and lemon juice to a shaker with ice.
3. Shake vigorously for 12 seconds until thoroughly cold.
4. Fine strain into the prepared coupe.
source: Ritz Hotel / Harry’s New York Bar, Paris (c. 1920)

name: Penicillin
description: Sam Ross’s 21st-century benchmark whiskey sour layering honey, fiery fresh ginger, and an aromatic Islay peated scotch float.
instructions:
1. Add blended scotch, fresh lemon juice, and honey-ginger syrup to a shaker with ice.
2. Shake hard for 12 seconds until cold.
3. Strain over fresh ice in a rocks glass.
4. Gently float peated Islay scotch over the back of a barspoon on top of the drink.
5. Garnish with candied ginger.

name: Paloma
description: Mexico’s beloved everyday highball pairing clean blanco tequila, fresh lime, and effervescent tart grapefruit soda.
instructions:
1. Rim a tall highball glass with coarse salt and fill with ice cubes.
2. Add blanco tequila, fresh lime juice, and a pinch of salt or drops of saline.
3. Top with cold grapefruit soda and stir gently.
4. Garnish with a fresh grapefruit slice or wedge.
source: Don Javier Delgado Corona, Tequila Mexico (c. 1950s)

name: Moscow Mule
description: The drink that sparked the American vodka revolution in 1941, delivering spicy ginger warmth and bright lime snap.
instructions:
1. Fill a copper mug or highball glass with crushed or cubed ice.
2. Add vodka and fresh lime juice.
3. Top with spicy ginger beer and stir gently to combine.
4. Garnish with a lime wheel and slapped mint sprig.

name: Tom Collins
description: The timeless sparkling gin lemonade highball, cooling bartenders and patrons since the 19th century.
instructions:
1. Add gin, fresh lemon juice, and simple syrup to a shaker with ice and shake briefly.
2. Strain into a tall Collins glass packed with ice.
3. Top with cold club soda and stir gently.
4. Garnish with a lemon wheel and a cherry.

name: Mint Julep
garnish: Generous mint bouquet with powdered sugar
description: The legendary drink of the Kentucky Derby, frosting a silver cup with robust bourbon, aromatic spearmint, and cracked ice.
instructions:
1. In a julep cup or rocks glass, gently press fresh mint leaves with demerara syrup to release aromatic oils without bruising.
2. Add bourbon and pack tightly with finely crushed ice.
3. Swizzle vigorously until the exterior of the cup frosts.
4. Top with a mound of crushed ice and garnish with a lush mint bouquet.

name: Mojito
description: Havana’s timeless highball balancing grassy white rum with fragrant spearmint, tart lime juice, and lively soda.
instructions:
1. Gently muddle mint leaves with simple syrup and lime juice in the base of a highball glass.
2. Add white rum and fill the glass with crushed ice.
3. Top with club soda and churn gently with a barspoon.
4. Crown with more crushed ice and slap a fresh mint sprig across the rim.

name: Aviation
description: Hugo Ensslin’s pre-Prohibition gem tinted a delicate sky-blue by crème de violette, offset by tart lemon and maraschino.
instructions:
1. Add gin, lemon juice, maraschino liqueur, and crème de violette to a cocktail shaker filled with ice.
2. Shake hard for 12-15 seconds until chilled.
3. Double strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Drop a brandied cherry into the base of the glass.

name: Corpse Reviver No. 2
description: Harry Craddock’s famous morning-after eye-opener delivering equal-parts precision with gin, Lillet, orange liqueur, and absinthe.
instructions:
1. Rinse a chilled coupe with absinthe and discard any excess.
2. Add gin, Cointreau, Lillet Blanc, and fresh lemon juice to a shaker with ice.
3. Shake hard for 12 seconds until thoroughly chilled.
4. Fine strain into the prepared coupe and garnish with an expressed lemon twist.

name: Americano
description: The gentler sparkling forebear to the Negroni, created at Gaspare Campari’s bar and championed by American tourists in Milan.
instructions:
1. Fill a highball glass with fresh ice.
2. Pour in equal parts Campari and sweet vermouth.
3. Top with cold club soda and give one gentle stir from bottom to top.
4. Garnish with a fresh orange half-wheel.

name: Vieux Carré
description: Walter Bergeron’s tribute to the New Orleans French Quarter, uniting rye, Cognac, sweet vermouth, Bénédictine, and dual bitters.
instructions:
1. Combine rye whiskey, Cognac, sweet vermouth, Bénédictine, and both bitters in a mixing glass with ice.
2. Stir thoroughly for 30 seconds until cold and glossy.
3. Strain into a rocks glass over a single large ice cube.
4. Express lemon peel oils over the glass and garnish.
source: Walter Bergeron, Carousel Bar New Orleans (1938)

name: Pisco Sour
description: The national drink of Peru, shaking grape brandy with tart lime, simple syrup, and egg white for a silken meringue crown.
instructions:
1. Add pisco, lime juice, simple syrup, and egg white to a shaker.
2. Dry shake without ice for 10 seconds to emulsify the albumen.
3. Add ice and shake hard for 12 seconds until frosty.
4. Double strain into a chilled coupe.
5. Drop 3 dots of Angostura bitters across the foam head.

name: Gimlet
description: The crisp Royal Navy sour pairing sharp botanical gin with bracing lime acidity and balanced sweetness.
instructions:
1. Combine gin, fresh lime juice, and simple syrup in a shaker with ice.
2. Shake hard for 12 seconds until well-chilled.
3. Fine strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Float a thin lime wheel on the surface.

name: Dark 'n Stormy
description: Bermuda’s maritime highball floating brooding black rum over effervescent spicy ginger beer, evoking a tempest at sea.
instructions:
1. Fill a tall highball glass with ice.
2. Pour in spicy ginger beer and fresh lime juice, then give a brief stir.
3. Carefully float blackstrap rum over the top using the back of a barspoon.
4. Garnish with a fresh lime wedge on the rim.

name: Paper Plane
garnish: Miniature paper plane or lemon twist
description: A modern four-part masterpiece created by Sam Ross, striking a sublime harmony between rich bourbon, bittersweet Aperol, herbal Amaro Nonino, and tart lemon.
instructions:
1. Add bourbon, Aperol, Amaro Nonino, and fresh lemon juice to a cocktail shaker filled with ice.
2. Shake hard for 12-15 seconds until thoroughly chilled and aerated.
3. Double strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Optionally garnish with a tiny origami paper plane perched on the rim.
source: Sam Ross, The Violet Hour / Milk & Honey (2007)

name: Naked and Famous
description: Joaquín Simó’s equal-parts gem blending earthy smoky mezcal with radiant Yellow Chartreuse, bittersweet Aperol, and brisk lime juice.
instructions:
1. Combine mezcal, Yellow Chartreuse, Aperol, and fresh lime juice in a shaker with cubed ice.
2. Shake vigorously until frosting forms on the tin.
3. Fine strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Garnish with a fresh lime wheel.

name: Bramble
description: Dick Bradsell’s quintessential 1980s London creation: crisp gin sour served over crushed ice with a cascading float of velvety blackberry liqueur.
instructions:
1. Add London dry gin, fresh lemon juice, and simple syrup to a shaker with ice and shake briefly.
2. Strain into an Old Fashioned glass packed with crushed ice.
3. Slowly drizzle blackberry liqueur over the crown of crushed ice to create a bleeding marbled effect.
4. Garnish with two fresh blackberries and a lemon half-wheel.

name: Jungle Bird
description: A dark, tropical revelation pairing robust blackstrap rum with luscious pineapple and the surprising bitter bite of Italian Campari.
instructions:
1. Combine blackstrap rum, Campari, fresh pineapple juice, fresh lime juice, and demerara syrup in a shaker.
2. Shake hard with ice for 15 seconds to create a creamy pineapple foam.
3. Strain over fresh crushed ice in an Old Fashioned glass or tiki goblet.
4. Fan pineapple fronds and skewer a cocktail cherry for garnish.
source: Jeffrey Ong, Aviary Bar, Kuala Lumpur Hilton (1973)

name: Tommy's Margarita
description: Julio Bermejo’s groundbreaking Californian recipe that strips away orange liqueur, letting pure 100% agave tequila shine alongside lime and agave nectar.
instructions:
1. Combine 100% agave blanco tequila, fresh lime juice, and agave nectar in a shaker with cubed ice.
2. Shake vigorously for 12 seconds until frosty.
3. Strain over fresh ice into a rocks glass (optionally half-rimmed with sea salt).
4. Garnish with a fresh lime wedge.
source: Julio Bermejo, Tommy's Mexican Restaurant, San Francisco (1990)

name: Oaxaca Old Fashioned
description: Phil Ward’s legendary Death & Co pioneer bridging reposado tequila and smoky mezcal under an aromatic cloud of flamed orange oils.
instructions:
1. Combine reposado tequila, mezcal, agave nectar, and Angostura bitters in a mixing glass filled with ice.
2. Stir patiently for 30 seconds until silky and cold.
3. Strain over a single large ice cube into an Old Fashioned glass.
4. Express and flame an orange peel over the glass, then drop it in.

name: Gin Basil Smash
description: Jörg Meyer’s vibrant emerald smash packing a garden-fresh bouquet of muddled basil leaves balanced by crisp London dry gin and bright lemon.
instructions:
1. Muddle a generous handful of fresh basil leaves with simple syrup in a cocktail shaker.
2. Add gin, lemon juice, and plenty of ice.
3. Shake violently until the herbs surrender their green oils and the tin is ice-cold.
4. Double strain through a fine mesh strainer over fresh ice into a rocks glass.
5. Garnish with a spapped basil top.

name: Industry Sour
description: A cult favorite among hospitality veterans combining equal parts Fernet-Branca and pungent Green Chartreuse into an intense, surprisingly harmonious sour.
instructions:
1. Combine Fernet-Branca, Green Chartreuse, fresh lime juice, and simple syrup in a shaker with ice.
2. Shake with maximum force for 15 seconds.
3. Fine strain into a chilled coupe glass.
4. Garnish with a lime twist expressed over the surface.

name: Division Bell
description: Phil Ward’s Pink Floyd-inspired Last Word sibling highlighting smoky mezcal, bittersweet Aperol, tart lime, and delicate maraschino notes.
instructions:
1. Combine mezcal, Aperol, maraschino liqueur, and fresh lime juice in an ice-filled shaker.
2. Shake well for 12 seconds.
3. Fine strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Twist a grapefruit peel over the surface and drop it in.

name: Left Hand
description: Sam Ross’s velvety evolution of the Boulevardier, anchoring fine bourbon and bitter Campari with chocolate bitters for a confectionary, seductive finish.
instructions:
1. Combine bourbon, Campari, sweet vermouth, and chocolate bitters in a mixing glass with ice.
2. Stir gently for 30 seconds until well chilled and integrated.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe glass.
4. Drop a brandied Luxardo cherry into the bottom.

name: White Negroni
description: Wayne Collins’s brilliant pale reimagining of the Negroni, trading red Campari and vermouth for earthy French gentian liqueur and golden Lillet Blanc.
instructions:
1. Add gin, Lillet Blanc, and Suze gentian liqueur to a mixing glass filled with ice.
2. Stir smoothly for 25-30 seconds until properly diluted and chilled.
3. Strain over a large ice rock into an Old Fashioned glass.
4. Express a swath of grapefruit peel over the rim and insert.

name: Trinidad Sour
description: An audacious modern miracle flipping traditional cocktail balance on its head by deploying a massive pour of Angostura Bitters as the primary base spirit.
instructions:
1. Add Angostura Bitters, rye whiskey, orgeat, and fresh lemon juice to a cocktail shaker.
2. Fill with solid ice cubes and shake vigorously for 15 seconds.
3. Double strain into a chilled coupe glass.
4. Garnish with a twist of lemon.
source: Valentino Bolognese, Angostura Global Cocktail Challenge (2009)

name: Revolver
description: Jon Santer’s rich San Francisco nightcap marrying high-rye bourbon with dark coffee liqueur and aromatic orange bitters.
instructions:
1. Add bourbon, coffee liqueur, and orange bitters to a mixing glass filled with cracked ice.
2. Stir for 25-30 seconds until thoroughly chilled and combined.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Flame an orange peel over the glass and float it atop.

name: Black Manhattan
description: Todd Smith’s dark, moody Manhattan variant replacing sweet vermouth with bittersweet Sicilian Amaro Averna.
instructions:
1. Combine rye whiskey, Amaro Averna, and both bitters in a mixing glass with plenty of ice.
2. Stir for 30 seconds until cold and silky.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe or cocktail glass.
4. Garnish with a brandied Luxardo cherry.
source: Todd Smith, Bourbon & Branch, San Francisco (2005)

name: Jasmine
description: Paul Harrington’s deceptive classic that tastes remarkably like fresh pink grapefruit juice despite containing none, built from gin, Campari, and Cointreau.
instructions:
1. Add gin, Campari, Cointreau, and fresh lemon juice to a shaker with ice.
2. Shake briskly for 12 seconds until chilled.
3. Double strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Garnish with an expressed lemon twist.
source: Paul Harrington, Townhouse Bar, Emeryville CA (c. 1990s)

name: Zombie
description: Don the Beachcomber’s legendary tiki juggernaut weaving three rums with citrus, cinnamon, falernum, and a haunting hint of absinthe.
instructions:
1. Combine light rum, dark rum, overproof rum, lime juice, grapefruit juice, cinnamon syrup, falernum, grenadine, absinthe, and Angostura bitters in a shaker with cracked ice.
2. Shake violently for 15 seconds.
3. Pour unstrained into a tall tiki mug or Collins glass.
4. Top with crushed ice and garnish lavishly with mint and a cinnamon stick.
source: Donn Beach, Don the Beachcomber, Hollywood (1934)

name: Painkiller
description: The British Virgin Islands icon balancing rich dark navy rum with lush pineapple, orange juice, and creamy coconut under a dusting of aromatic nutmeg.
instructions:
1. Combine dark rum, pineapple juice, orange juice, and cream of coconut in a shaker with crushed ice.
2. Shake hard for 15 seconds to emulsify the coconut.
3. Pour into a tall glass or tiki mug filled with fresh crushed ice.
4. Generously grate fresh whole nutmeg over the top and garnish with a pineapple wedge.
source: Daphne Henderson, Soggy Dollar Bar, Jost Van Dyke (1970s)

name: Piña Colada
description: Puerto Rico’s national cocktail blending crisp white rum, sweet cream of coconut, and fresh pineapple juice into a velvety frozen tropical escape.
instructions:
1. Add white rum, cream of coconut, and fresh pineapple juice into a blender with a scoop of crushed ice.
2. Blend on high speed for 20 seconds until silky and smooth.
3. Pour into a chilled hurricane or highball glass.
4. Garnish with a fresh pineapple triangle and maraschino cherry.
source: Ramón "Monchito" Marrero, Caribe Hilton, San Juan (1954)

name: Caipirinha
description: Brazil’s vibrant national cocktail showcasing grassy, rustic sugarcane cachaça muddled vigorously with fresh lime quarters and sugar.
instructions:
1. Cut a fresh lime into small wedges and place in a double rocks glass.
2. Add simple syrup or fine sugar and muddle vigorously to express juice and essential peel oils.
3. Fill the glass with cracked ice and pour in the cachaça.
4. Stir well to integrate the sugar and garnish with lime wheels.

name: Ti' Punch
description: The soul of the French Caribbean: Martinique’s minimalist ritual uniting raw floral Rhum Agricole with cane syrup and a lime disc.
instructions:
1. Add cane sugar syrup or demerara syrup to a small tumbler.
2. Cut a small disc of lime peel with a little flesh and squeeze it into the glass.
3. Add unaged Rhum Agricole.
4. Stir with a bois lélé swizzle stick or barspoon.
5. Enjoy at room temperature or with a single ice cube.

name: Three Dots and a Dash
garnish: Three cocktail cherries and a pineapple frond
description: Don the Beachcomber’s WWII victory tribute—Morse code for "V"—marrying grassy agricole and dark rums with warm honey and allspice.
instructions:
1. Combine Rhum Agricole, dark rum, lime juice, orange juice, honey syrup, falernum, and allspice dram in a shaker with cracked ice.
2. Shake vigorously for 15 seconds.
3. Fine strain into a chilled coupe or goblet.
4. Garnish with three skewered maraschino cherries and a pineapple spear (three dots and a dash).

name: Navy Grog
description: A formidable maritime tiki staple balancing three heavy rums against tart lime, bittersweet grapefruit, and rich honey syrup.
instructions:
1. Add light rum, dark rum, and Demerara rum with lime juice, grapefruit juice, honey syrup, and a splash of club soda to a shaker with ice.
2. Shake hard for 12 seconds.
3. Strain over a solid ice cone in a double rocks glass.
4. Insert a straw directly through the ice cone.

name: Singapore Sling
description: The historic Raffles Hotel creation delivering a botanical cascade of gin, cherry liqueur, Bénédictine, and sparkling effervescence.
instructions:
1. Combine gin, Cherry Heering, Cointreau, Bénédictine, pineapple juice, lime juice, grenadine, and bitters in an ice-filled shaker.
2. Shake hard for 15 seconds until cold and foamy.
3. Strain into a tall highball glass filled with ice.
4. Top with club soda and garnish with fresh pineapple and cherry.
source: Ngiam Tong Boon, Long Bar, Raffles Hotel (c. 1915)

name: Saturn
garnish: Lemon peel ring surrounding a cherry
description: One of the rare world-class gin-based tiki cocktails, matching London dry gin with passion fruit, orgeat, and spicy falernum.
instructions:
1. Add gin, lemon juice, passion fruit syrup, orgeat, and falernum to a cocktail shaker with crushed ice.
2. Shake vigorously for 15 seconds until well-chilled.
3. Fine strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Garnish with a circular lemon peel resembling planetary rings pierced with a cocktail cherry.
source: J. "Popo" Galsini, IBA World Championship winner (1967)

name: Corn 'n Oil
description: Barbados’s straightforward, brooding favorite floating dark molasses-rich blackstrap rum over spicy clove-forward falernum and lime.
instructions:
1. In a rocks glass filled with crushed ice, add falernum and fresh lime juice.
2. Stir briefly to chill.
3. Float blackstrap rum gently over the top to resemble dark crude oil floating on golden liquid.
4. Add a dash of Angostura bitters and garnish with lime.

name: Fog Cutter
description: Trader Vic’s potent restorative combining white rum, cognac, and gin with citrus and almond, finished with a crown of cream sherry.
instructions:
1. Combine light rum, cognac, gin, lemon juice, orange juice, and orgeat in a shaker with ice.
2. Shake hard for 15 seconds.
3. Pour unstrained into a tall tiki mug or Collins glass.
4. Float dry sherry over the top and garnish with mint and orange.

name: Blue Hawaii
description: The mid-century Waikiki phenomenon bathing rum, vodka, and pineapple in the vivid aquamarine hue of blue curaçao.
instructions:
1. Combine white rum, vodka, blue curaçao, pineapple juice, and sweet & sour in an ice-filled shaker.
2. Shake for 12 seconds until icy.
3. Strain over fresh crushed ice into a tall hurricane glass.
4. Garnish with a pineapple wedge and paper umbrella.
source: Harry Yee, Kaiser Hawaiian Village Hotel, Waikiki (1957)

name: Hurricane
description: New Orleans’s French Quarter legend shaking generous measures of light and dark rum with tart lemon juice and luscious passion fruit syrup.
instructions:
1. Combine dark rum, light rum, passion fruit syrup, lemon juice, orange juice, and grenadine in a shaker with crushed ice.
2. Shake hard for 12 seconds.
3. Pour into a signature curved hurricane glass.
4. Garnish with an orange slice and maraschino cherry.

name: Hotel Nacional Special
description: Havana’s golden age coupe highlighting crisp Cuban-style rum, velvety apricot liqueur, and fresh pineapple frothed to an airy foam.
instructions:
1. Combine white rum, fresh pineapple juice, fresh lime juice, apricot liqueur, and simple syrup in a shaker.
2. Shake hard with ice for 15 seconds to develop a thick, velvety head of pineapple foam.
3. Double strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Garnish with a thin lime wheel floated in the foam.
source: Wil P. Taylor, Hotel Nacional de Cuba, Havana (1930s)

name: Hemingway Daiquiri
description: Crafted for Ernest Hemingway at El Floridita, doubling down on white rum with tart pink grapefruit and Italian maraschino liqueur in place of sugar.
instructions:
1. Combine white rum, fresh lime juice, grapefruit juice, and maraschino liqueur in a shaker with plenty of ice.
2. Shake hard for 12 seconds until thoroughly cold.
3. Double strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Garnish with a lime wheel and cherry.
source: Constantino Ribalaigua Vert, El Floridita, Havana (c. 1930s)

name: Martinez
description: The profound evolutionary bridge between the Manhattan and the Dry Martini, combining sweet vermouth, malty Old Tom gin, and maraschino.
instructions:
1. Add Old Tom gin, sweet vermouth, maraschino liqueur, and bitters to a mixing glass filled with ice.
2. Stir smoothly for 30 seconds until cold and blended.
3. Strain into a chilled Nick & Nora glass.
4. Express lemon peel oils over the surface.
source: O.H. Byron, The Modern Bartenders' Guide (1884)

name: Hanky Panky
description: Ada Coleman’s historic 1903 Savoy Hotel gem, elevating equal parts gin and sweet vermouth with a medicinal dash of bitter Fernet-Branca.
instructions:
1. Combine gin, sweet vermouth, and Fernet-Branca in a mixing glass with ice.
2. Stir patiently for 30 seconds.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Express orange peel oils over the drink and garnish.
source: Ada Coleman, American Bar, Savoy Hotel London (1903)

name: Bee's Knees
description: Prohibition ingenuity at its finest, softening botanical gin with soothing honey syrup and tart fresh lemon juice.
instructions:
1. Combine gin, fresh lemon juice, and honey syrup in a cocktail shaker filled with ice.
2. Shake hard for 12 seconds.
3. Double strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Garnish with an expressed lemon twist.

name: Southside
description: The aristocratic country club and speakeasy standard delivering a crisp gin sour perfumed with muddled aromatic mint.
instructions:
1. Add fresh mint leaves and simple syrup to a shaker and gently press with a muddler.
2. Add gin, lime juice, and ice.
3. Shake hard for 12 seconds.
4. Double strain through a fine mesh strainer into a chilled coupe.
5. Float a fresh mint leaf on the surface.

name: Clover Club
description: A pre-Prohibition Philadelphia gentlemen’s club signature featuring gin, lemon, raspberry syrup, and an ethereal silky egg white foam.
instructions:
1. Combine gin, dry vermouth, lemon juice, raspberry syrup, and egg white in a shaker without ice and dry shake vigorously for 15 seconds to emulsify.
2. Add ice and shake hard for another 15 seconds to chill.
3. Fine strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Garnish with skewered raspberries.

name: Blood and Sand
description: Inspired by Rudolph Valentino’s 1922 bullfighter film, weaving smoky scotch with sweet vermouth, cherry liqueur, and orange juice.
instructions:
1. Add Scotch whisky, sweet vermouth, Cherry Heering, and fresh orange juice to a shaker filled with ice.
2. Shake vigorously for 15 seconds.
3. Double strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Express an orange peel twist over the rim.
source: Harry Craddock, The Savoy Cocktail Book (1930)

name: Rob Roy
description: The Scottish counterpart to the Manhattan, substituting blended Scotch whisky for rye to yield a smoky, rich, and sophisticated sipper.
instructions:
1. Combine Scotch whisky, sweet vermouth, and Angostura bitters in an ice-filled mixing glass.
2. Stir smoothly for 30 seconds until cold and properly diluted.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe or cocktail glass.
4. Garnish with a brandied Luxardo cherry.

name: White Lady
description: Harry MacElhone’s timeless Parisian classic marrying London dry gin with orange triple sec and fresh lemon under a pillowy foam.
instructions:
1. Add gin, Cointreau, lemon juice, and egg white into a shaker.
2. Dry shake without ice for 10 seconds, then add ice and shake hard until ice-cold.
3. Fine strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Garnish with a thin lemon peel.
source: Harry MacElhone, Harry's New York Bar, Paris (1919)

name: Monkey Gland
description: An iconic 1920s Paris concoction enlivening gin and orange juice with rich grenadine and an alluring rinse of absinthe.
instructions:
1. Rinse a chilled coupe with absinthe and discard the excess.
2. In an ice-filled shaker, combine gin, fresh orange juice, and real pomegranate grenadine.
3. Shake hard for 12 seconds.
4. Strain into the prepared coupe and garnish with an orange twist.
source: Harry MacElhone, Harry's New York Bar, Paris (c. 1920s)

name: Mary Pickford
description: Crafted at the Hotel Nacional in Havana during Prohibition for Americas Sweetheart, shaking white rum with pineapple, maraschino, and grenadine.
instructions:
1. Combine white rum, fresh pineapple juice, maraschino liqueur, and grenadine in a shaker with ice.
2. Shake vigorously for 15 seconds.
3. Double strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Drop a cocktail cherry into the bottom.

name: Scofflaw
description: Created during American Prohibition at Harry's New York Bar in Paris to salute law-flouting imbibers, pairing rye with dry vermouth, lemon, and grenadine.
instructions:
1. Add rye whiskey, dry vermouth, fresh lemon juice, grenadine, and orange bitters to an ice-filled shaker.
2. Shake hard for 12 seconds.
3. Fine strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Garnish with a flamed orange peel.

name: Brandy Alexander
description: The indulgent after-dinner classic combining French cognac with dark crème de cacao and heavy cream, crowned with fragrant grated nutmeg.
instructions:
1. Combine cognac, crème de cacao, and heavy cream in a cocktail shaker with ice.
2. Shake with vigor for 15 seconds until completely integrated and ice-cold.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Grate fresh nutmeg across the silky foam surface.

name: Ramos Gin Fizz
description: Henry C. Ramos’s legendary New Orleans masterpiece, whipped with cream, egg white, citrus, and orange flower water into an architectural meringue tower.
instructions:
1. Add gin, lemon juice, lime juice, simple syrup, heavy cream, egg white, and orange flower water to a shaker.
2. Dry shake without ice for 30-45 seconds.
3. Add ice cubes and shake vigorously for 60 seconds until frosty and thick.
4. Strain into a tall highball glass without ice.
5. Pour club soda down the center to slowly push the stiff foam crown past the glass rim.
source: Henry C. Ramos, Imperial Cabinet Saloon, New Orleans (1888)

name: Between the Sheets
description: A heady variation on the Sidecar marrying equal measures of cognac and white rum with orange triple sec and lemon.
instructions:
1. Add cognac, white rum, Cointreau, and fresh lemon juice to a shaker with ice.
2. Shake hard for 12 seconds until thoroughly chilled.
3. Fine strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Flame a lemon peel over the top and discard or float.
source: Harry MacElhone, Harry's New York Bar, Paris (c. 1930)

name: Casino
description: Hugo Ensslin’s crisp Aviation sibling featuring Old Tom gin, maraschino, fresh lemon juice, and orange bitters.
instructions:
1. Combine Old Tom gin, maraschino liqueur, fresh lemon juice, and orange bitters in an ice-filled cocktail shaker.
2. Shake vigorously for 12 seconds.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Garnish with a maraschino cherry and lemon twist.
source: Hugo Ensslin, Recipes for Mixed Drinks (1916)

name: Garibaldi
description: The Italian two-ingredient icon named for general Giuseppe Garibaldi, blending red Campari with high-speed frothed fluffy orange juice.
instructions:
1. Fill a tall highball glass with ice.
2. Pour in Campari.
3. Juice fresh oranges at high speed in a blender or juicer until thick and frothy.
4. Pour the aerated orange juice over the Campari.
5. Garnish with a fresh orange wedge on the rim.
source: Italian Classic / Revived by Dante NYC (c. 1860s / 2015)

name: Negroni Sbagliato
description: A sparkling happy mistake created in Milan when bartender Mirko Stocchetto accidentally grabbed Prosecco instead of gin for a Negroni.
instructions:
1. Fill a rocks glass or wine goblet with large ice cubes.
2. Add Campari and sweet vermouth, then stir briefly.
3. Top with chilled Prosecco sparkling wine.
4. Gently stir once from the bottom to integrate without losing carbonation.
5. Garnish with an orange wheel.

name: Cynar Spritz
garnish: Castelvetrano green olive or orange slice
description: A Venetian favorite trading Aperol for the savory, earthy, and bittersweet botanicals of artichoke-based Cynar amaro.
instructions:
1. Fill a wine glass or rocks glass with ice.
2. Add Cynar and Prosecco.
3. Top with a splash of sparkling soda water.
4. Stir gently and garnish with an orange slice or a green olive.

name: Bicicletta
description: The timeless northern Italian cafe refresher named after old men who swerved home on their bicycles after enjoying a couple on sunny afternoons.
instructions:
1. Fill a wine glass or rocks glass with ice.
2. Pour in Campari and crisp dry Italian white wine.
3. Top with chilled club soda and stir gently.
4. Garnish with a fresh lemon wheel.

name: Cardinale
description: Rome’s sleek variation on the Negroni substituting sweet vermouth with bone-dry French vermouth for a crisp, scarlet aperitif.
instructions:
1. Combine gin, dry vermouth, and Campari in an ice-filled mixing glass.
2. Stir smoothly for 30 seconds until cold.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe or over ice in a rocks glass.
4. Express lemon peel oils over the surface.

name: Lucien Gaudin
description: Named for the legendary 1920s French Olympic fencing champion, bridging the Negroni and White Lady with gin, Campari, Cointreau, and dry vermouth.
instructions:
1. Add gin, Campari, Cointreau, and dry vermouth to an ice-filled mixing glass.
2. Stir for 25-30 seconds until thoroughly chilled and integrated.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Garnish with an expressed orange twist.

name: Toronto
description: David Embury’s refined rye whiskey cocktail utilizing pungent Fernet-Branca as a profound bittering accent balanced with a hint of syrup.
instructions:
1. Combine rye whiskey, Fernet-Branca, simple syrup, and Angostura bitters in a mixing glass with ice.
2. Stir steadily for 30 seconds until cold.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Express an orange peel over the glass and insert.
source: David Embury, The Fine Art of Mixing Drinks (1948)

name: Adonis
description: An elegant low-ABV Victorian classic from Broadway, uniting equal parts rich sweet sherry and sweet vermouth with aromatic orange bitters.
instructions:
1. Combine sweet oloroso sherry, sweet vermouth, and orange bitters in an ice-filled mixing glass.
2. Stir gently for 30 seconds until cold.
3. Strain into a chilled Nick & Nora glass.
4. Express orange peel oils over the surface.

name: Bamboo
description: Louis Eppinger’s historic Yokohama masterpiece pairing dry sherry with dry vermouth and bitters for a bone-dry, saline aperitif.
instructions:
1. Add fino or manzanilla dry sherry, dry vermouth, and both bitters to a mixing glass filled with ice.
2. Stir smoothly for 30 seconds.
3. Strain into a chilled Nick & Nora glass.
4. Express lemon peel oils across the rim.

name: Sherry Cobbler
description: The 19th-century sensation that popularized the drinking straw and cocktail shaker, serving dry sherry with sugar and muddled fruit over crushed ice.
instructions:
1. In a shaker, muddle orange slices with simple syrup.
2. Add dry sherry and ice, shake briefly to chill.
3. Pour unstrained into an Old Fashioned glass or highball packed with crushed ice.
4. Garnish lavishly with berries, citrus wheels, and a straw.

name: Pimm's No. 1 Cup
garnish: Cucumber slice, mint, strawberry & lemon wheel
description: The definitive British summer garden party cup, pairing herbal Pimm's liqueur with effervescent ginger ale and a lush harvest of fresh fruits.
instructions:
1. Fill a tall highball glass with ice, sliced cucumber, strawberries, and mint leaves.
2. Add Pimm's No. 1 and fresh lemon juice.
3. Top with chilled ginger ale or sparkling lemonade.
4. Stir gently to integrate all ingredients.

name: Hugo Spritz
description: Also known as the Elderflower Spritz, this breezy South Tyrolean alpine spritz unites elderflower liqueur, sparkling Prosecco, soda, and torn mint.
instructions:
1. Add fresh mint leaves and elderflower liqueur to a wine glass and gently press.
2. Fill the glass with ice cubes.
3. Pour in chilled Prosecco and a splash of sparkling club soda.
4. Stir gently from the bottom and garnish with a mint sprig and lime.

name: Blackthorn
description: A stately late-19th century Irish whiskey Manhattan variant laced with dry vermouth, Angostura bitters, and a perfume of absinthe.
instructions:
1. Add Irish whiskey, dry vermouth, absinthe, and Angostura bitters to a mixing glass filled with ice.
2. Stir smoothly for 30 seconds.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Express lemon peel oils over the surface.

name: Rabo de Galo
description: Brazil’s beloved bittersweet everyday classic, marrying fiery sugarcane cachaça with sweet Italian vermouth and herbal amaro.
instructions:
1. Combine cachaça, sweet vermouth, and Cynar in a rocks glass with ice.
2. Stir steadily for 20 seconds.
3. Express an orange twist over the glass and insert.

name: Milano-Torino (Mi-To)
description: The venerable 1860s foundation of the entire Negroni dynasty, marrying Milan’s bitter red Campari with Turin’s sweet vermouth.
instructions:
1. Fill a rocks glass with ice cubes.
2. Add equal measures of Campari and sweet vermouth.
3. Stir gently for 15 seconds to chill and integrate.
4. Garnish with a fresh orange slice.

name: Vesper
garnish: Large thin slice of lemon peel
description: James Bond’s iconic creation from Casino Royale: three measures of Gordon’s gin, one of vodka, half of Kina Lillet, shaken until ice-cold.
instructions:
1. Add London dry gin, vodka, and Lillet Blanc into a cocktail shaker packed with ice.
2. Shake violently until ice chips form on the surface.
3. Strain into a chilled deep goblet or martini glass.
4. Garnish with a long, thin lemon peel spiral.

name: Rusty Nail
description: The Rat Pack favorite uniting smoky Scotch whisky with honeyed, heather-scented Drambuie herbal liqueur over a single rock.
instructions:
1. Fill an Old Fashioned glass with a single large ice cube.
2. Pour in Scotch whisky and Drambuie.
3. Stir gently for 20 seconds.
4. Express a twist of lemon over the glass and drop it in.

name: Godfather
description: A smooth 1970s staple pairing peaty Scotch whisky with the rich toasted almond sweetness of Italian amaretto.
instructions:
1. Add Scotch whisky and amaretto into an Old Fashioned glass with ice cubes.
2. Stir slowly for 20 seconds to blend.
3. Express an orange peel over the glass and drop it in.
source: 1970s Classic (named after the film The Godfather)

name: White Russian
garnish: No garnish or whole coffee bean
description: The decadent after-dinner drink elevated to pop-culture immortality by The Big Lebowski, layering rich cream over vodka and coffee liqueur.
instructions:
1. Fill an Old Fashioned glass with fresh ice cubes.
2. Pour in vodka and coffee liqueur and stir briefly.
3. Gently float heavy cream or whole milk over the back of a barspoon.
4. Stir before drinking or sip layered.

name: Black Russian
description: Created for the American ambassador to Luxembourg, matching neutral crisp vodka with dark bittersweet Mexican coffee liqueur.
instructions:
1. Add vodka and coffee liqueur into an Old Fashioned glass filled with ice.
2. Stir well for 20 seconds to dilute and chill.
3. Garnish with a cocktail cherry.

name: El Diablo
description: Trader Vic’s dazzling highball cascading dark blackcurrant cassis over reposado tequila, fresh lime, and spicy effervescent ginger beer.
instructions:
1. Combine reposado tequila and fresh lime juice in a shaker with ice and shake briefly.
2. Strain into a tall highball glass filled with ice.
3. Top with spicy ginger beer.
4. Carefully float Crème de Cassis over the top to create a rich crimson halo.
5. Garnish with a lime wedge.

name: Japanese Cocktail
description: Jerry Thomas’s historic 1862 creation marrying velvety French cognac with aromatic orgeat syrup and heavy dashes of Angostura bitters.
instructions:
1. Add cognac, orgeat, and Angostura bitters to a mixing glass filled with ice.
2. Stir smoothly for 30 seconds.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Express a lemon twist over the drink and drop it in.
source: Jerry Thomas, How to Mix Drinks (1862)

name: French Connection
description: An alluring 1970s two-ingredient digestif pairing rich warming French cognac with sweet Italian amaretto liqueur.
instructions:
1. Combine equal parts cognac and amaretto in an Old Fashioned glass with a large ice cube.
2. Stir gently for 20 seconds.
3. Express an orange twist over the glass and insert.
source: 1970s Classic (named after the Gene Hackman film)

name: Brandy Milk Punch
description: New Orleans’s festive brunch and holiday staple blending rich brandy and bourbon with whole milk, vanilla sweetness, and fresh nutmeg.
instructions:
1. Add cognac or bourbon, whole milk or cream, simple syrup, and a drop of vanilla extract into a shaker with cracked ice.
2. Shake hard for 20 seconds until well chilled and foamy.
3. Strain into an Old Fashioned glass filled with fresh ice.
4. Dust generously with fresh grated nutmeg.

name: Bloody Mary
garnish: Celery stalk, lemon wedge & green olive
description: The legendary savory brunch restorative balancing crisp vodka with seasoned tomato juice, lemon, Worcestershire, hot sauce, and celery salt.
instructions:
1. Roll (pour back and forth between two shaker tins with ice) vodka, tomato juice, lemon juice, Worcestershire sauce, hot sauce, black pepper, and celery salt.
2. Strain into a tall highball glass filled with ice.
3. Garnish with a tall leafy celery stalk, lemon wedge, and an olive.
source: Fernand Petiot, Harry's New York Bar, Paris (1921)

name: French 77
description: An elegant floral riff on the classic French 75, substituting elderflower liqueur for gin alongside crisp lemon and Champagne.
instructions:
1. Add elderflower liqueur and fresh lemon juice to a shaker tin with ice.
2. Shake briefly until chilled.
3. Strain into a chilled champagne flute.
4. Top with chilled dry sparkling wine.
5. Express the oils from a lemon peel twist over the glass and garnish.

name: St-Germain Cocktail
description: The signature aperitif crafted to showcase elderflower liqueur with dry white sparkling wine and soda water.
instructions:
1. Fill a tall wine glass or Collins glass with fresh ice.
2. Add St-Germain elderflower liqueur.
3. Top with brut Champagne or dry sparkling wine and club soda.
4. Stir gently once to combine.
5. Garnish with a lemon twist.

name: Monte Cassino
description: An equal-parts modern craft benchmark created by Damon Dyer at Flatiron Lounge, marrying rye whiskey with herbal monastic liqueurs and crisp lemon.
instructions:
1. Add rye whiskey, Bénédictine, Yellow Chartreuse, and fresh lemon juice to a cocktail shaker filled with ice.
2. Shake vigorously for 12-15 seconds until well-chilled.
3. Fine strain into a chilled coupe glass.
4. Express the oils of a lemon twist over the surface and drop into the drink.

name: Little Italy
description: Audrey Saunders' beloved Manhattan variation featuring bittersweet artichoke amaro Cynar in place of standard aromatic bitters.
instructions:
1. Combine rye whiskey, sweet vermouth, and Cynar in a mixing glass with ice.
2. Stir thoroughly for 25-30 seconds until ice-cold and silky.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe or Nick & Nora glass.
4. Garnish with a cocktail cherry.

name: Greenpoint
description: A stellar Brooklyn neighborhood variation on the Manhattan created at Milk & Honey, pairing spicy rye with honeyed Yellow Chartreuse.
instructions:
1. Combine rye whiskey, Yellow Chartreuse, sweet vermouth, and bitters in a mixing glass filled with ice.
2. Stir for 25-30 seconds until well-chilled.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Express lemon twist oils over the glass and garnish.

name: Ferrari
description: The iconic bartender handshake cocktail combining equal parts Campari and Fernet-Branca into an intensely bittersweet, minty-citrus digestive blast.
instructions:
1. Pour Campari and Fernet-Branca directly into a rocks glass over a single large ice cube.
2. Stir gently to integrate.
3. Express an orange peel over the surface and garnish.

name: Chet Baker
description: Sam Ross's sultry rum tribute to jazz trumpeter Chet Baker, marrying aged rum, sweet vermouth, honey, and aromatic bitters.
instructions:
1. Add aged rum, sweet vermouth, honey syrup, and Angostura bitters into a mixing glass with ice.
2. Stir until properly chilled and diluted.
3. Strain into a rocks glass over a large ice cube.
4. Express orange peel oils over the surface and insert.

name: Kingston Negroni
description: A bold Negroni variation replacing gin with high-ester Jamaican overproof pot-still rum, created by Joaquín Simó at Death & Co.
instructions:
1. Add Jamaican overproof rum, Campari, and sweet vermouth to a mixing glass with ice.
2. Stir thoroughly until well-chilled.
3. Strain into a double rocks glass over a large clear ice cube.
4. Express an orange peel over the drink and garnish.

name: Right Hand
description: Michael McIlroy's aged rum counterpart to the Left Hand, balancing rich cane oak, bitter Campari, sweet vermouth, and chocolate bitters.
instructions:
1. Add aged rum, Campari, sweet vermouth, and chocolate bitters to a mixing glass filled with ice.
2. Stir for 25-30 seconds until well-chilled.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Drop a cocktail cherry into the glass.

description: A spicy, cacao-scented evolution of the Boulevardier created at The Violet Hour, commemorating the Whiskey Rebellion of 1794.
instructions:
1. Add rye whiskey, Campari, sweet vermouth, and chocolate bitters to a mixing glass filled with cracked ice.
2. Stir for 25 seconds until very cold.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe glass.
4. Express an orange peel twist over the rim and garnish.
source: Toby Maloney, The Violet Hour Chicago (c. 2007)

name: Gold Rush
description: A modern classic whiskey sour variation created at Milk & Honey that substitutes silky honey syrup for simple syrup.
instructions:
1. Add bourbon, fresh lemon juice, and honey syrup to a cocktail shaker filled with ice.
2. Shake vigorously for 12-15 seconds until well-chilled.
3. Strain into a rocks glass over a single large ice cube.
4. Garnish with a fresh lemon wheel.

name: Enzoni
description: An ingenious hybrid of the Negroni and Gin Sour created by Vincenzo Errico, featuring crushed fresh green grapes that soften bitter Campari.
instructions:
1. In a cocktail shaker, gently muddle 5 green grapes in simple syrup.
2. Add gin, Campari, fresh lemon juice, and ice.
3. Shake vigorously for 15 seconds until frosty.
4. Double strain into a rocks glass packed with crushed or cubed ice.
5. Garnish with skewered green grapes.

name: Siesta
description: A modern craft agave staple created by Katie Stipe, combining crisp blanco tequila with bittersweet Campari, tart grapefruit, and lime.
instructions:
1. Add blanco tequila, Campari, fresh grapefruit juice, fresh lime juice, and simple syrup to an ice-filled shaker.
2. Shake hard for 12 seconds.
3. Fine strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Garnish with a fresh grapefruit wheel or twist.

name: French Pearl
description: Audrey Saunders' aromatic Pegu Club gem, balancing crisp botanical gin with cool mint, lime juice, and a delicate anise whisper of absinthe.
instructions:
1. Gently muddle fresh mint leaves with simple syrup in a cocktail shaker.
2. Add gin, fresh lime juice, absinthe, and ice cubes.
3. Shake vigorously for 12-15 seconds.
4. Double strain into a chilled coupe.
5. Float a fresh mint leaf on the surface.

name: 21st Century
description: Jim Meehan's clever PDT update to the 20th Century cocktail, substituting blanco tequila for gin to create an exquisite agave, cacao, and lemon harmony.
instructions:
1. Combine blanco tequila, white crème de cacao, and fresh lemon juice in a shaker with ice.
2. Shake hard for 12 seconds until well-frosted.
3. Fine strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Dust the surface with dark chocolate shavings.

name: Old Cuban
description: Audrey Saunders' luxurious modern classic crossing a Mojito with a French 75, pairing aged rum and mint with a sparkling Champagne crown.
instructions:
1. Gently muddle mint leaves with simple syrup and lime juice in a shaker.
2. Add aged rum, Angostura bitters, and ice cubes.
3. Shake hard for 12 seconds until cold.
4. Fine strain into a chilled coupe or flute.
5. Top with brut Champagne or dry sparkling wine.
6. Float a fresh mint leaf for garnish.

name: Gordon's Cup
description: A savory, garden-crisp modern staple muddling fresh cucumber discs and lime wedges with London dry gin, sea salt, and cracked black pepper.
instructions:
1. In the bottom of a rocks glass, muddle cucumber slices and lime wedges with simple syrup.
2. Add London dry gin and a pinch of sea salt.
3. Fill the glass with cracked or crushed ice.
4. Stir gently to lift ingredients from the base.
5. Garnish with a fresh grind of black pepper and a cucumber wheel.

name: Tia Mia
description: Ivy Mix's smoky Brooklyn Mai Tai split between funky Jamaican rum and artisanal mezcal, backed by rich orgeat and dry orange curaçao.
instructions:
1. Combine mezcal, Jamaican rum, fresh lime juice, orange curaçao, and orgeat in a cocktail shaker with ice.
2. Shake hard for 12 seconds.
3. Strain over crushed ice into a double rocks glass.
4. Invert a spent lime wheel half and nestle a slapped mint bouquet inside.
source: Ivy Mix, Lani Kai / Leyenda NYC (2010)

name: Medicina Latina
description: A Latin American agave adaptation of Sam Ross's Penicillin, shaking blanco tequila with ginger, honey, and lime, crowned with a smoky mezcal float.
instructions:
1. Add blanco tequila, fresh lime juice, ginger syrup, and honey syrup to a shaker with ice.
2. Shake vigorously for 12 seconds.
3. Strain into a rocks glass over a single large ice cube.
4. Gently float smoky mezcal over the top using the back of a barspoon.
5. Garnish with candied ginger on a pick.

name: Bitter Giuseppe
description: Stephen Cole's low-ABV amaro masterpiece built around Cynar, accented by sweet vermouth, fresh lemon juice, and aromatic orange bitters.
instructions:
1. Combine Cynar, sweet vermouth, fresh lemon juice, and orange bitters in a mixing glass with ice.
2. Stir for 25-30 seconds until thoroughly chilled.
3. Strain into a rocks glass filled with fresh ice cubes.
4. Express lemon peel oils over the glass and insert.
source: Stephen Cole, The Violet Hour Chicago (c. 2008)

name: Trinidad Especial
description: Agostino Perrone's award-winning riff on the Trinidad Sour, pairing aromatic bitters and orgeat with floral Peruvian pisco and lime juice.
instructions:
1. Combine Angostura bitters, pisco, orgeat, and fresh lime juice in a shaker with plenty of ice.
2. Shake hard for 15 seconds.
3. Fine strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Garnish with a floating lime wheel.
source: Agostino Perrone, The Connaught Bar London (2008)

name: Queen's Park Swizzle
description: The crown jewel of Trinidadian cocktails created at the Queen's Park Hotel in the 1920s: rich Demerara rum swizzled with mint, lime, and crushed ice beneath an aromatic crown of Angostura.
instructions:
1. In a highball glass, gently press mint leaves with demerara syrup and fresh lime juice.
2. Add Demerara rum and fill glass two-thirds full with crushed ice.
3. Insert a swizzle stick or barspoon and spin rapidly between your palms until the outside of the glass frosts over.
4. Pack with more crushed ice and dash Angostura bitters liberally across the crown to create a two-tone gradient.
5. Garnish with a lush mint bouquet.
source: Queen's Park Hotel, Port of Spain, Trinidad (c. 1920s)

name: Tradewinds
description: A decadent 1970s tropical wonder blending dark and light rums with apricot liqueur, creamy coconut, and fresh lemon juice over crushed ice.
instructions:
1. Combine blackstrap rum, light rum, apricot liqueur, cream of coconut, and fresh lemon juice in a shaker with crushed ice.
2. Shake hard for 12 seconds.
3. Pour unstrained into a tall highball glass or tiki goblet.
4. Top with additional crushed ice and garnish with slapped mint and a lemon wheel.

name: Missionary's Downfall
description: Don the Beachcomber's legendary pastel-green blend of light rum, peach liqueur, fresh mint leaves, honey, pineapple, and lime.
instructions:
1. Add light rum, peach liqueur, fresh lime juice, honey syrup, pineapple juice, and a large handful of fresh mint to a shaker with crushed ice.
2. Shake hard for 15 seconds to incorporate the mint and chill thoroughly.
3. Fine strain into a chilled coupe or goblet filled with crushed ice.
4. Garnish with a fresh mint bouquet.

name: Scorpion
description: Trader Vic's potent Polynesian communal bowl adapted for single service, uniting light rum and French cognac with orgeat and citrus juices.
instructions:
1. Combine light rum, cognac, fresh orange juice, fresh lemon juice, and orgeat in a shaker with crushed ice.
2. Shake vigorously for 15 seconds.
3. Pour unstrained into a tall tiki mug or Collins glass.
4. Pack with extra crushed ice.
5. Garnish with an orange slice and maraschino cherry.

name: Port Light
description: A rare tropical classic built on Kentucky bourbon rather than rum, sweetened with passion fruit syrup, grenadine, and lemon juice.
instructions:
1. Combine bourbon, passion fruit syrup, fresh lemon juice, grenadine, and egg white in a shaker.
2. Dry shake without ice for 10 seconds to create foam.
3. Add crushed ice and shake hard for 12 seconds.
4. Strain into a rocks glass packed with crushed ice.
5. Garnish with a cocktail cherry.

name: Ancient Mariner
description: Jeff 'Beachbum' Berry's modern tiki tour-de-force fusing Demerara and Jamaican rums with tart grapefruit, lime, and aromatic allspice dram.
instructions:
1. Combine Demerara rum, dark Jamaican rum, fresh lime juice, fresh grapefruit juice, simple syrup, and allspice dram in a cocktail shaker.
2. Fill with crushed ice and shake hard for 12-15 seconds.
3. Pour unstrained into a double Old Fashioned glass.
4. Top with additional crushed ice and garnish with a lime wheel and mint sprig.

name: Test Pilot
description: Don the Beachcomber's potent aeronautical tribute layering two rums with Cointreau, falernum, absinthe, and Angostura bitters.
instructions:
1. Combine dark Jamaican rum, light rum, Cointreau, velvet falernum, lime juice, absinthe, and Angostura bitters in a shaker with crushed ice.
2. Shake hard for 10-12 seconds.
3. Pour unstrained into a highball glass or tiki mug.
4. Pack with additional crushed ice and garnish with a cocktail cherry.

name: Cobra's Fang
description: A serpentine tiki masterpiece from Don the Beachcomber balancing overproof 151 rum and dark rum with exotic passion fruit, falernum, and absinthe.
instructions:
1. Add 151 proof rum, dark rum, velvet falernum, passion fruit syrup, fresh lime juice, orange juice, absinthe, and grenadine to a shaker with crushed ice.
2. Shake vigorously for 12 seconds.
3. Pour into a tall curved glass or tiki mug over crushed ice.
4. Garnish with a lime wheel and slapped mint sprig.

name: Jet Pilot
description: Steve Crane's high-octane supersonic upgrade to the Test Pilot, packing three rums, cinnamon syrup, falernum, grapefruit, and absinthe.
instructions:
1. Combine dark Jamaican rum, gold rum, 151 proof rum, velvet falernum, lime juice, grapefruit juice, cinnamon syrup, absinthe, and Angostura in a shaker with crushed ice.
2. Shake hard for 12 seconds.
3. Pour into a double Old Fashioned glass filled with crushed ice.
4. Garnish with a cocktail cherry and lime wheel.
source: Steve Crane, The Luau, Beverly Hills (1958)

name: Halekulani
description: A 1930s Hawaiian hotel classic bringing bourbon into paradise with pineapple, orange, lemon, and rich demerara grenadine.
instructions:
1. Combine bourbon, pineapple juice, orange juice, fresh lemon juice, grenadine, and Angostura bitters in an ice-filled shaker.
2. Shake vigorously for 12-15 seconds until very cold.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Garnish with a fresh lemon wheel on the rim.

name: Suffering Bastard
description: Created by Joe Scialom during World War II as an anti-hangover restorative, pairing gin and bourbon with lime juice, bitters, and spicy ginger beer.
instructions:
1. Combine gin, bourbon, fresh lime juice, and Angostura bitters in a cocktail shaker with ice.
2. Shake briefly to chill.
3. Pour into a tall highball glass or Collins glass.
4. Top with cold ginger beer and stir gently.
5. Garnish with a fresh mint sprig and cucumber wheel.

name: Castaway
description: A simple yet surprisingly addictive mid-century tropical highball balancing gold rum with rich coffee liqueur and tart pineapple juice.
instructions:
1. Add gold rum, coffee liqueur, and pineapple juice to a shaker filled with ice.
2. Shake hard for 12 seconds until frosty and foamed.
3. Strain over fresh ice into a tall highball glass.
4. Garnish with a fresh pineapple wedge.

name: La Rosita
description: A refined Mexican Negroni variation pairing reposado tequila with Campari and a split balance of sweet and dry vermouths.
instructions:
1. Combine reposado tequila, Campari, sweet vermouth, dry vermouth, and Angostura bitters in a mixing glass with ice.
2. Stir for 25-30 seconds until cold and silky.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe or rocks glass over ice.
4. Express lemon peel oils over the surface and garnish.

name: Mezcalita
description: A smoky, terroir-driven Margarita variation showcasing artisanal mezcal with Cointreau, fresh lime, and a drizzle of agave nectar.
instructions:
1. Rim half of a rocks glass with chili-salt or coarse sea salt.
2. Combine mezcal, Cointreau, fresh lime juice, and agave nectar in a shaker filled with ice.
3. Shake hard for 12 seconds until icy.
4. Strain over fresh ice into the prepared rocks glass.
5. Garnish with a fresh lime wheel.

name: Bijou
description: Harry Johnson's luminous 19th-century jewel cocktail named for its sparkling colors: gin for diamonds, vermouth for rubies, and Green Chartreuse for emeralds.
instructions:
1. Add London dry gin, sweet vermouth, Green Chartreuse, and orange bitters to a mixing glass filled with ice.
2. Stir smoothly for 30 seconds until ice-cold.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe or Nick & Nora glass.
4. Garnish with a cocktail cherry or expressed lemon twist.

name: Remember the Maine
description: Charles H. Baker Jr.'s robust Manhattan variation commemorating the sunken USS Maine, adding sweet Cherry Heering and an absinthe rinse.
instructions:
1. Rinse a chilled coupe with absinthe and discard any excess.
2. In a mixing glass, combine rye whiskey, sweet vermouth, and Cherry Heering with ice.
3. Stir for 25-30 seconds until cold and diluted.
4. Strain into the prepared coupe.
5. Garnish with a cocktail cherry.
source: Charles H. Baker Jr., The Gentleman's Companion (1939)

name: Bobby Burns
description: A rich Scottish tribute to poet Robert Burns, combining blended Scotch whisky and sweet vermouth with the herbal, honeyed depth of Bénédictine.
instructions:
1. Combine blended Scotch whisky, sweet vermouth, and Bénédictine in a mixing glass filled with ice.
2. Stir thoroughly for 25-30 seconds until well-chilled.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe or Nick & Nora.
4. Express lemon twist oils over the glass and serve with shortbread.

name: Old Pal
description: Harry MacElhone's brisk, drier sibling to the Boulevardier, swapping sweet vermouth for crisp French dry vermouth alongside rye and Campari.
instructions:
1. Combine rye whiskey, dry vermouth, and Campari in a mixing glass with ice.
2. Stir for 25 seconds until very cold.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Express lemon twist oils over the rim and garnish.
source: Harry MacElhone, Harry's New York Bar Paris (1927)

name: Champs-Élysées
description: An aristocratic French sour combining fine cognac with the complex alpine botanicals of Green Chartreuse, fresh lemon, and Angostura bitters.
instructions:
1. Add cognac, Green Chartreuse, fresh lemon juice, simple syrup, and Angostura bitters to a shaker with ice.
2. Shake hard for 12 seconds.
3. Fine strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Garnish with an expressed lemon peel twist.
source: Harry Craddock, The Savoy Cocktail Book (1930)

name: Tipperary
description: An Irish whiskey classic balancing rich triple-distilled malt with sweet vermouth, vibrant Green Chartreuse, and orange bitters.
instructions:
1. Add Irish whiskey, sweet vermouth, Green Chartreuse, and orange bitters to a mixing glass filled with ice.
2. Stir thoroughly for 25-30 seconds.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Express an orange twist over the surface and drop it in.
source: Hugo Ensslin, Recipes for Mixed Drinks (1916)

name: 20th Century
description: C.A. Tuck's streamlined 1937 masterpiece shaking botanical gin with aromatized Lillet Blanc, white crème de cacao, and tart lemon juice.
instructions:
1. Combine London dry gin, Lillet Blanc, white crème de cacao, and fresh lemon juice in a shaker with ice.
2. Shake hard for 12 seconds until frosty.
3. Fine strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Express lemon twist oils over the glass and garnish.
source: C.A. Tuck, Café Royal Cocktail Book (1937)

name: Alaska
description: A golden, spirituous Pre-Prohibition icon blending London dry gin with the honeyed herbal warmth of Yellow Chartreuse and orange bitters.
instructions:
1. Combine London dry gin, Yellow Chartreuse, and orange bitters in a mixing glass filled with ice.
2. Stir for 25-30 seconds until ice-cold.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe or Nick & Nora.
4. Express lemon twist oils over the rim and garnish.

name: New York Sour
description: The visual and textural pinnacle of whiskey sours, floating dry red wine over a chilled bourbon sour to add fruit acidity and striking color contrast.
instructions:
1. Combine rye whiskey or bourbon, fresh lemon juice, and simple syrup in a cocktail shaker filled with ice.
2. Shake hard for 12 seconds until thoroughly chilled.
3. Strain over fresh ice into a rocks glass.
4. Gently pour dry red wine over the back of a barspoon to create a floating red layer.
5. Garnish with a lemon wheel and cocktail cherry.

name: Metropolitan
description: A rich Victorian-era Manhattan adaptation trading whiskey for French brandy or cognac, sweetened with sweet vermouth and bitters.
instructions:
1. Add brandy or cognac, sweet vermouth, simple syrup, and bitters to a mixing glass filled with ice.
2. Stir smoothly for 25-30 seconds until cold.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Garnish with a brandied cocktail cherry.

name: Palmetto
description: A classic Cuban-American crossover built as a Rum Manhattan with aged rum, sweet vermouth, and orange bitters.
instructions:
1. Combine aged rum, sweet vermouth, and orange bitters in a mixing glass with ice.
2. Stir for 25-30 seconds until ice-cold.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe or Nick & Nora.
4. Express an orange twist over the surface and drop it in.

name: Artillery
description: A formidable 19th-century soldier's cocktail pairing London dry gin and sweet vermouth with maraschino liqueur and an absinthe rinse.
instructions:
1. Rinse a chilled coupe with absinthe.
2. Combine gin, sweet vermouth, maraschino liqueur, and bitters in a mixing glass with ice.
3. Stir for 25-30 seconds until cold.
4. Strain into the prepared coupe.
5. Garnish with a cocktail cherry and orange twist.

name: Gin Fizz
description: The primordial effervescent refresher of the late 1800s: gin, crisp lemon, and sugar shaken hard and poured over ice with a bubbling fountain of soda.
instructions:
1. Combine gin, fresh lemon juice, and simple syrup in a cocktail shaker filled with ice.
2. Shake hard for 15 seconds until very cold.
3. Strain into a tall highball or fizz glass without ice (or over fresh ice cubes).
4. Top with cold club soda and give a brief lift with a barspoon.
5. Garnish with a lemon wheel.

name: Southside Fizz
description: The effervescent highball edition of the Southside, lifting botanical gin, fresh lime, and aromatic spearmint with cold club soda.
instructions:
1. Combine gin, fresh lime juice, simple syrup, and fresh mint leaves in a shaker filled with ice.
2. Shake vigorously for 12 seconds.
3. Fine strain into a tall highball glass packed with fresh ice.
4. Top with cold club soda and stir gently once.
5. Garnish with a slapped mint sprig and lime wheel.

name: Dirty Martini
description: The beloved savory classic accenting crisp gin with dry French vermouth and salty olive brine.
instructions:
1. Add gin, dry vermouth, and olive brine to a mixing glass filled with ice.
2. Stir thoroughly for 25-30 seconds until ice-cold and properly diluted.
3. Fine strain into a chilled martini glass.
4. Garnish with an olive on a pick.

name: Gibson
description: An elegant, silky dry martini riff distinguished by the subtle savory sweetness of a pickled cocktail pearl onion.
instructions:
1. Combine gin and dry vermouth in a mixing glass filled with cracked ice.
2. Stir briskly for 30 seconds until thoroughly chilled and diluted.
3. Strain into a chilled martini glass or coupe.
4. Garnish with a cocktail pearl onion on a pick.
source: Charles Dana Gibson / Players Club NYC (c. 1900s)

name: Michelada
description: A restorative Mexican beer cocktail spiked with tart fresh lime, fiery hot sauce, savory Worcestershire, and chilled crisp lager.
instructions:
1. Run a cut lime wedge around the rim of a tall chilled glass and dip in chili-salt.
2. Fill glass with fresh ice cubes.
3. Add fresh lime juice, Worcestershire sauce, hot sauce, and a pinch of salt.
4. Top slowly with chilled Mexican lager.
5. Give a gentle single stir to integrate and garnish with a lime wheel.

name: Green Park
description: A vibrant London craft standard blending herbaceous fresh basil with London dry gin, lemon, and silky egg white foam.
instructions:
1. Drop fresh basil leaves into the shaker tin and muddle gently to release oils.
2. Add gin, lemon juice, simple syrup, and egg white.
3. Dry shake vigorously without ice for 10 seconds to emulsify.
4. Add ice and shake hard for another 12 seconds until frosty.
5. Double strain into a chilled coupe and float a small basil leaf on the foam.
source: Erik Lorincz, The American Bar at The Savoy London (2011)

name: Dirty Mezcalita
description: An earthy, smoky agave sour laced with savory olive brine and rich orange liqueur over rocks.
instructions:
1. Rim half of a rocks glass with chili-salt or sea salt.
2. Combine mezcal, Cointreau, fresh lime juice, olive brine, and agave nectar in a shaker with ice.
3. Shake hard for 12 seconds until thoroughly chilled.
4. Strain over fresh ice into the prepared rocks glass.
5. Garnish with a fresh lime wheel.

name: Chartreuse Swizzle
description: A modern cult classic featuring Green Chartreuse swizzled with tropical pineapple, fresh lime, and spicy falernum over crushed ice.
instructions:
1. In a tall Collins or highball glass, combine Green Chartreuse, pineapple juice, fresh lime juice, and falernum.
2. Fill glass two-thirds full with crushed ice.
3. Insert a swizzle stick (or barspoon) and spin rapidly between palms until frost forms on the outside of the glass.
4. Top with additional crushed ice to form a mound.
5. Garnish with a generous fresh mint bouquet and freshly grated nutmeg.
source: Marco Dionysos, Smuggler's Cove San Francisco (c. 2002)

name: Metropole
description: An elegant pre-Prohibition Manhattan variant showcasing rich French brandy or cognac paired with dry vermouth, Peychaud's, and aromatic bitters.
instructions:
1. Combine cognac, dry vermouth, simple syrup, and both bitters in a mixing glass with ice.
2. Stir thoroughly for 25-30 seconds until ice-cold and properly diluted.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe or cocktail glass.
4. Express lemon peel oils or garnish with a brandied cherry.

name: Apium
garnish: Fresh mint sprig or cucumber slice
description: A crisp, botanical savory cooler highlighting London dry gin shaken with fresh celery juice, lime, and cooling spearmint.
instructions:
1. Combine gin, fresh lime juice, fresh celery juice, simple syrup, and mint leaves in a cocktail shaker.
2. Fill shaker with ice and shake vigorously for 12 seconds.
3. Double strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Garnish with a fresh mint sprig.

name: Paris Is Burning
description: A smoldering, bittersweet modern classic marrying earthy mezcal, crisp dry gin, elderflower liqueur, and bitter gentian Suze.
instructions:
1. Combine mezcal, London dry gin, St-Germain, and Suze in a mixing glass filled with cracked ice.
2. Stir briskly for 25-30 seconds until ice-cold.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Express a lemon peel over the surface and drop it into the glass.

name: Royal Bermuda Yacht Club
description: An aristocratic Caribbean sour upgrading the classic Daiquiri with aged Barbados rum, spiced velvet falernum, Cointreau, and fresh lime.
instructions:
1. Combine aged rum, velvet falernum, fresh lime juice, and Cointreau in a cocktail shaker.
2. Fill with ice and shake hard for 10-12 seconds until thoroughly chilled.
3. Fine strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Garnish with a fresh lime wheel.

name: Flannel Shirt
description: The ultimate cozy autumn nightcap layering peaty blended Scotch with apple cider, bitter amaro Averna, and warm spice.
instructions:
1. Combine blended Scotch, apple cider, amaro Averna, lemon juice, rich demerara syrup, and St. Elizabeth Allspice Dram in a mixing glass with ice.
2. Stir thoroughly for 25 seconds until chilled.
3. Strain into a rocks glass over a single large cube of ice.
4. Express fresh orange peel oils over the surface and garnish.

name: Stone Fence
description: One of America's oldest historical potables, spiking crisp, effervescent hard cider with spicy rye whiskey and Angostura bitters.
instructions:
1. Fill a tall highball glass with fresh ice cubes.
2. Add rye whiskey and two dashes of Angostura bitters.
3. Top gently with chilled dry hard cider.
4. Stir lightly once to combine and garnish with an apple slice or lemon wheel.

name: Brandy Crusta
garnish: Full sugar rim & wide lemon horse's neck peel
description: The flamboyant 1850s New Orleans progenitor to the Sidecar, featuring fine cognac, curaçao, Maraschino, and a continuous sugar-crusted rim.
instructions:
1. Moisten the outside rim of a chilled coupe or small wine glass and roll in superfine sugar to create a wide crust.
2. Line the inside wall of the glass with a long, wide spiral lemon horse's neck peel.
3. In an ice-filled shaker, combine cognac, curaçao, lemon juice, Maraschino liqueur, simple syrup, and Boker's/Angostura bitters.
4. Shake vigorously for 12 seconds.
5. Fine strain into the prepared crusted glass.
source: Joseph Santini, City Exchange New Orleans (c. 1850s)

name: Shoulder Season
description: A cozy, cold-weather Old Fashioned riff balancing spicy rye and rich apple brandy with maple syrup, aromatic Angostura, and black walnut bitters.
instructions:
1. Combine rye whiskey, apple brandy, maple syrup, Angostura bitters, and walnut bitters in a mixing glass with ice.
2. Stir thoroughly for 25-30 seconds until well-chilled and integrated.
3. Strain into a rocks glass over a large ice cube.
4. Garnish with a freshly cut apple slice.

name: Monte Carlo
description: A decadent rye Manhattan riff swapping vermouth for herbal, honeyed Bénédictine liqueur and aromatic Peychaud's bitters.
instructions:
1. Combine rye whiskey, Bénédictine, and Angostura bitters in a mixing glass with cracked ice.
2. Stir thoroughly for 25-30 seconds until ice-cold.
3. Strain over a single large ice cube into an old fashioned rocks glass.
4. Express lemon peel oils over the surface and drop peel into the drink.
source: David Embury, The Fine Art of Mixing Drinks (1948)

name: À La Louisienne
description: A legendary New Orleans Creole masterpiece blending spicy rye whiskey with sweet vermouth, herbal Bénédictine, Peychaud's, and absinthe.
instructions:
1. Combine rye whiskey, sweet vermouth, Bénédictine, absinthe, and Peychaud's bitters in a mixing glass filled with ice.
2. Stir smoothly for 30 seconds until thoroughly chilled and integrated.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe or cocktail glass.
4. Garnish with a brandied cocktail cherry.
source: Restaurant de la Louisiane, New Orleans (c. 1930s)

name: Mexican Firing Squad
description: A spicy, vibrant 1930s Mexican craft classic shaking 100% agave tequila with tart lime, rich pomegranate grenadine, and aromatic Angostura.
instructions:
1. Combine blanco tequila, fresh lime juice, real pomegranate grenadine, and Angostura bitters in a cocktail shaker with ice.
2. Shake hard for 12 seconds until frosty.
3. Strain over fresh ice into a rocks glass.
4. Garnish with a fresh lime wheel and cherry.
source: Charles H. Baker Jr., The Gentleman's Companion (1937)

name: Artichoke Hold
description: A brilliant modern amaro sour pairing bitter Cynar with funky Jamaican overproof rum, floral St-Germain, lime, and rich almond orgeat.
instructions:
1. Add Cynar, Jamaican overproof rum, St-Germain, fresh lime juice, and orgeat to a shaker with ice.
2. Shake vigorously for 12 seconds.
3. Fine strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Slap a fresh mint sprig and float as garnish.

name: Blinker
description: A brisk, bright 1930s high-proof sour pairing spicy rye whiskey with freshly squeezed tart grapefruit juice and sweet raspberry syrup.
instructions:
1. Combine rye whiskey, fresh grapefruit juice, and raspberry syrup in an ice-filled shaker.
2. Shake hard for 12 seconds until thoroughly cold.
3. Fine strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Express grapefruit oils over the drink and discard or trim twist.
source: Patrick Gavin Duffy, The Official Mixer's Manual (1934)

name: Brown Derby
description: The Hollywood Golden Age classic pairing warm Kentucky bourbon with fresh bittersweet pink grapefruit and rich wildflower honey syrup.
instructions:
1. Combine bourbon, fresh grapefruit juice, and honey syrup in a shaker with ice.
2. Shake vigorously for 12 seconds until icy.
3. Double strain into a chilled cocktail coupe.
4. Express fresh grapefruit peel twist over the rim.
source: Vendôme Club / Brown Derby, Los Angeles (1930s)

name: Red Hook
description: The brooding modern Brooklyn borough classic matching spicy rye whiskey with rich, bittersweet Punt e Mes vermouth and dry Maraschino.
instructions:
1. Add rye whiskey, Punt e Mes (sweet vermouth), and Maraschino liqueur to a mixing glass filled with ice.
2. Stir smoothly for 25-30 seconds until ice-cold and properly diluted.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Garnish with a brandied cocktail cherry.

name: Diamondback
description: A potent Baltimore pre-Prohibition powerhouse melding spicy rye whiskey with bonded apple brandy and herbal Yellow Chartreuse.
instructions:
1. Combine rye whiskey, apple brandy (Applejack), and Yellow Chartreuse in a mixing glass with cracked ice.
2. Stir thoroughly for 25-30 seconds until cold and diluted.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Garnish with a brandied cherry.

name: Fancy Free
description: An opulent, nut-and-cherry accented Old Fashioned riff pairing rich bourbon with dry Maraschino liqueur and dual citrus bitters.
instructions:
1. Combine bourbon, Maraschino liqueur, Angostura bitters, and orange bitters in a mixing glass filled with ice.
2. Stir briskly for 25 seconds until thoroughly chilled.
3. Strain into a rocks glass over a single large ice cube.
4. Express fresh orange peel oils over the glass and drop it in.

name: Brooklyn
description: The seminal outer-borough Manhattan cousin pairing spicy rye whiskey with crisp dry vermouth, Maraschino, and bitter gentian Amer Picon.
instructions:
1. Combine rye whiskey, dry vermouth, Maraschino liqueur, and Amer Picon in a mixing glass filled with cracked ice.
2. Stir smoothly for 30 seconds until ice-cold and diluted.
3. Strain into a chilled cocktail coupe.
4. Garnish with a brandied cherry.

name: El Presidente
description: The aristocrat of 1920s Havana, stirring light Cuban-style white rum with delicate blanc vermouth, dry curaçao, and real pomegranate grenadine.
instructions:
1. Add white rum, blanc vermouth, dry curaçao, and grenadine to a mixing glass filled with ice.
2. Stir gracefully for 25-30 seconds until frosty and silky.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Express fresh orange oils over the rim and garnish with a brandied cherry.

name: Air Mail
