description: An effervescent Caribbean celebration shaking golden aged rum with tart lime juice and rich honey syrup, topped with dry sparkling wine.
instructions:
1. Combine aged rum, fresh lime juice, and honey syrup in a shaker with ice.
2. Shake hard for 10-12 seconds until cold.
3. Strain into a chilled Champagne flute or coupe.
4. Top gently with chilled dry sparkling wine.
5. Garnish with a thin lime wheel.

name: Twelve Mile Limit
description: A daring 1934 Prohibition triple-spirit sour combining white rum, spicy rye, and French cognac with fresh lemon and pomegranate grenadine.
instructions:
1. Combine white rum, rye whiskey, cognac, fresh lemon juice, and grenadine in a cocktail shaker.
2. Fill with ice and shake hard for 12 seconds.
3. Double strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Garnish with a lemon twist.

name: Jack Rose
description: An indelible pre-Prohibition American standard balancing historic bonded applejack with tart fresh lemon and rich pomegranate grenadine.
instructions:
1. Combine applejack, fresh lemon juice, and real pomegranate grenadine in a shaker with ice.
2. Shake vigorously for 12 seconds until frosty.
3. Fine strain into a chilled cocktail coupe.
4. Garnish with a thin apple slice or lemon twist.

name: Harvey Wallbanger
description: The breezy 1970s California retro icon elevating fresh orange juice and crisp vodka with an aromatic float of golden Galliano vanilla liqueur.
instructions:
1. Fill a tall highball glass with fresh ice cubes.
2. Add vodka and fresh orange juice, then stir well to combine.
3. Float Galliano over the back of a barspoon on top of the drink.
4. Garnish with an orange wheel and cherry on a pick.
source: Donato 'Duke' Antone, Blackwatch Bar Sunset Strip (c. 1950s)

name: Hot Toddy
garnish: Lemon wheel studded with cloves & cinnamon stick
description: The time-honored winter restorative blending warming whiskey with steaming water, fragrant honey, fresh lemon, and aromatic winter spices.
instructions:
1. Warm a mug by filling with boiling water for 30 seconds, then discard.
2. Add whiskey, honey, and fresh lemon juice to the mug.
3. Top with boiling water and stir thoroughly until the honey dissolves.
4. Garnish with a clove-studded lemon wheel and a whole cinnamon stick.

name: Gin Rickey
description: Washington D.C.'s official historic cooler delivering absolute botanical refreshment with gin, fresh lime, and effervescent club soda.
instructions:
1. Fill a tall highball glass with cracked ice.
2. Squeeze the juice of half a lime into the glass and drop the spent shell in.
3. Add London dry gin.
4. Top with cold, highly carbonated club soda and give a brief gentle stir.

name: Presbyterian
description: A snappy turn-of-the-century thirst quencher pairing rich whiskey with equal parts sparkling ginger ale and crisp club soda.
instructions:
1. Fill a tall highball glass with fresh ice cubes.
2. Pour in bourbon or blended Scotch whisky.
3. Top with equal parts chilled ginger ale and club soda.
4. Stir gently once to integrate without losing effervescence.
5. Garnish with an expressed lemon peel twist.

name: Pegu Club
description: This classic gin cocktail was invented in the 1920s at the Pegu Club in Yangon, Myanmar. It's essentially a Gin Sour by way of a Sidecar.
instructions:
1. Combine all ingredients in a shaker with ice.
2. Shake until cold and diluted.
3. Strain into a chilled glass.

name: Army & Navy
description: This orgeat gin sour from the 1940s was made popular at the Army and Navy Club in Washington, D.C.
instructions:
1. Combine all ingredients in a shaker with ice.
2. Shake until cold and diluted.
3. Strain into a chilled glass.
source: Army and Navy Club, Washington D.C. (c. 1940s)

name: Rosita
description: The Rosita reads like a tequila Negroni, but calls for reposado tequila at its base and cuts the typical sweet vermouth portion with dry vermouth.
instructions:
1. Combine all ingredients in a mixing glass with ice.
2. Stir for 20-30 seconds until well-chilled.
3. Strain into a rocks glass filled with ice.
4. Express orange twist and discard.
5. Garnish with a dehydrated orange wheel.

name: Sea Legs
description: The Sea Legs cocktail encapsulates a nautical feel without the kitsch. Big smoke flavor from the scotch and mezcal is lightened up with fresh lime and almond orgeat. And don't skip the celery bitters on this one.
instructions:
1. Add all ingredients to a cocktail shaker.
2. Add ice and shake hard for 10 seconds.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe glass with salted rim.
4. Garnish with a lime wheel.

name: Overhand Smash
description: Take Pimm's No. 1 further with this perfect summer patio cooler.
instructions:
1. In a mixing tin, muddle sliced cucumber and basil.
2. Add elderflower, gin, Pimm's, lime, and bitters.
3. Shake to chill and mix well.
4. Pour over ice into a highball glass.
5. Top with ginger beer.
6. Garnish with fresh fruit, cucumbers.

name: Death Or Glory
description: Created around 2012 by award-winning bartender Abigail Gullo at SoBou in the French Quarter. An unapologetically bold, modern riff on the Negroni.
instructions:
1. In a cocktail shaker filled with ice, combine the Aperol, mezcal, and vermouth.
2. Add 4-6 drops of bitters.
3. Stir until well-chilled.
4. Strain into a glass with one large ice cube.

name: French Blonde
description: This citrusy, complex cocktail is a favorite of pop icon Taylor Swift. Low ABV relative to its complexity, it delivers bright floral and grapefruit character in a surprisingly elegant package.
instructions:
1. Fill a shaker with ice and add Lillet Blanc, gin, grapefruit juice, elderflower liqueur, and lemon bitters.
2. Shake vigorously for at least 30 seconds.
3. Double strain into a chilled Nick & Nora glass.
4. Garnish with a lemon or orange peel.

name: Cherry Picker
description: The Cherry Picker highlights the note of cherry found within bourbon while paying homage to the Manhattan. A touch of Maraschino Liqueur amplifies fresh cherry while being softened by notes of vanilla, caramel, and toasted oak.
instructions:
1. Combine all ingredients into a mixing glass with ice.
2. Stir until cold, about 30 seconds.
3. Strain into a chilled rocks glass over a large ice cube.
4. Express an orange peel over the top and garnish with a cherry.

name: Storm King
description: Storm King Art Center is a vast sculpture park in the Hudson Valley whose autumn foliage draws devoted visitors each fall. This cocktail is an equally marvelous autumn mix of blended Scotch, nocino, Bénédictine, and Angostura. It's a spin on a Manhattan by way of both the Rob Roy and the Bobby Burns.
instructions:
1. Add all ingredients into a mixing glass with ice and stir until well-chilled.
2. Strain into a chilled coupe glass.
3. Garnish with skewered brandied cherries.

name: Improved Japanese
description: Riffing on a 19th-century classic from Jerry Thomas's Bar Tenders Guide, the Improved Japanese Cocktail gets a boost from the addition of lemon juice and Peychaud's bitters.
instructions:
1. Add cognac, orgeat, lemon juice, and bitters to a mixing glass filled with ice.
2. Stir smoothly for 30 seconds.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Express a lemon twist over the drink and drop it in.

name: King Kong
description: A deliciously funky, tropical spin on the Old Fashioned from Sam Ross. Bourbon meets the high-ester funk of Jamaican rum and the rich sweetness of banana liqueur stirred over a large cube.
instructions:
1. Combine bourbon, Jamaican rum, crème de banane, and bitters in a mixing glass filled with ice.
2. Stir well until chilled and diluted.
3. Strain into a rocks glass over a large ice cube.
4. Express a lemon peel over the drink and use as garnish.
source: Sam Ross, Attaboy, New York City (2015)

name: Intercontinental
description: Created by Duggan McDonnell at Cantina in San Francisco, the Intercontinental takes you around the world with ingredients native to France (Armagnac), Italy (Averna), and Croatia (Maraschino). Equal parts, bittersweet, and entirely spirit-forward.
instructions:
1. Combine all ingredients in a mixing glass filled with ice.
2. Stir well until chilled.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Garnish with an orange or lemon twist.

name: Apple Blossom
description: A spring stirred cocktail from Jeffrey Morganthaler. Apple brandy and bourbon share the base, softened by Lillet Blanc and Bénédictine, with a single dash of Angostura to keep it honest. A riff in the spirit of the Vieux Carré.
instructions:
1. Combine all ingredients in a mixing glass with ice.
2. Stir to chill, about 30 seconds.
3. Strain into a chilled rocks glass over ice cubes.
4. Garnish with a lemon twist.

name: L'Amour Banane
description: Bold, funky, and lush. Overproof Jamaican rum brings the heat, while banana liqueur and Yellow Chartreuse add rich, herbal sweetness, and pineapple and lemon keep the whole thing from getting too serious.
instructions:
1. Add all ingredients to a shaker tin.
2. Add ice and shake until chilled.
3. Strain into a glass over a large cube.
4. Garnish with a banana leaf or lemon twist.

name: Lady Luck
description: Created by Danielle Tatarin of The Designer Cocktail Company, featured in British Columbia's Taste magazine for signature wedding cocktails. Gin, elderflower, pear, and lemon, finished with grapefruit bitters for structure.
instructions:
1. Pour all ingredients into a cocktail shaker with ice.
2. Shake well then strain into a chilled coupe.
3. Garnish with a pear fan and serve.

name: Perfect Manhattan
description: In classic mixology, "Perfect" means equal parts dry and sweet vermouth. This Manhattan is drier and more nuanced than the standard recipe, letting the rye push through while the two vermouths add dimension rather than sweetness.
instructions:
1. Combine rye whiskey, vermouths, and bitters in an ice-filled mixing glass.
2. Stir smoothly for 30 seconds.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Garnish with a brandied cocktail cherry.

name: Whiskey Lullaby
description: A soul-soothing nightcap from Janessa Flowers at Watershed Distillery. Bourbon as the base, Averna for body and richness, Bénédictine for mouthfeel, and Nocino for nuttiness. Stirred and strained over a large cube.
instructions:
1. Combine all ingredients in a mixing glass with ice.
2. Stir until cold and diluted.
3. Strain into a rocks glass over a large ice cube.
4. Express lemon peel over the top and garnish.

name: Hot Buttered Rum
description: A colonial American restorative dating to the 17th century. Aged rum meets a warm blend of butter, brown sugar, cinnamon, nutmeg, orange zest, and vanilla. A perfect cold-weather drink built for sitting by a fire.
instructions:
1. In a warm mug, stir to combine melted butter, brown sugar, cinnamon, nutmeg, and orange zest.
2. Add vanilla extract and rum, stir again.
3. Carefully pour in boiling water.
4. Stir to combine and garnish with a cinnamon stick.

name: Cabaret
description: A variation on the original Cabaret from Harry Craddock's Savoy Cocktail Book (1930).
instructions:
1. Combine all ingredients in a mixing glass with ice.
2. Stir until well-chilled, about 25 seconds.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Garnish with a lemon twist.
source: Harry Craddock, The Savoy Cocktail Book (1930), adapted

name: Razzle Dazzle
description: A bright, berry-forward vodka spritz from Watershed Distillery. Raspberry liqueur and Peychaud's bitters give it a pink hue and a bitter snap, finished with sparkling wine for lift.
instructions:
1. Combine vodka, raspberry liqueur, lemon juice, simple syrup, and bitters in a shaker with ice.
2. Shake well.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Top with sparkling wine.
5. Garnish with raspberries.

name: Trident
description: A savory, bittersweet modern classic by Robert Hess that matches the caraway and dill of Scandinavian aquavit with herbal Cynar and bone-dry Manzanilla sherry.
instructions:
1. Combine aquavit, Cynar, dry sherry, and peach bitters in a mixing glass filled with ice.
2. Stir for 25-30 seconds until well-chilled and integrated.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe or Nick & Nora glass.
4. Express lemon peel oils over the surface and garnish.

name: Vampiro
description: A spicy, savory Mexican highball from San Luis Soyatlán, Jalisco, mixing tequila with citrus, savory tomato, fiery hot sauce, and sparkling grapefruit soda.
instructions:
1. Rim a highball glass with lime and chili-salt or coarse salt, then fill with fresh ice.
2. Add tequila, tomato juice, orange juice, lime juice, Worcestershire sauce, hot sauce, and a pinch of salt.
3. Stir gently to integrate.
4. Top with chilled grapefruit soda and garnish with a lime wheel.

name: Kamikaze
description: A crisp 1970s classic and the direct predecessor to the Cosmopolitan, balancing crisp vodka with triple sec and tart fresh lime.
instructions:
1. Combine vodka, triple sec, and fresh lime juice in a cocktail shaker filled with ice.
2. Shake vigorously for 10-12 seconds until frosty and cold.
3. Strain into a chilled shot glass (or into a coupe for a full cocktail).
4. Garnish with a lime wedge.

name: B-52
description: A famous 1970s layered shooter featuring distinct floating tiers of rich coffee liqueur, velvety Irish cream, and sweet orange cognac liqueur.
instructions:
1. Pour coffee liqueur directly into the bottom of a shot glass.
2. Invert a bar spoon with the tip touching the inside glass wall just above the coffee layer.
3. Slowly pour Irish cream over the back of the spoon to create a clean middle layer.
4. Repeat the float with Grand Marnier on top.
5. Serve immediately.

name: Dublin Drop
description: A famous drop-shot boilermaker traditionally known as the Irish Car Bomb or Irish Slammer, pairing Irish whiskey and Irish cream dropped into a half pint of dry Irish stout.
instructions:
1. Fill a highball or pint glass with half a pint (6 oz) of chilled dry Irish stout.
2. In a separate shot glass, combine equal parts Irish whiskey and Baileys Irish cream.
3. Drop the shot glass directly into the stout.
4. Drink immediately in continuous sips before the cream curdles.

name: Pickleback
description: A Brooklyn dive-bar phenomenon pairing a sharp pour of Irish whiskey with an immediate chaser of salty, tangy dill pickle brine.
instructions:
1. Pour Irish whiskey into a shot glass.
2. Pour chilled dill pickle brine into a second shot glass.
3. Shoot the whiskey first, then immediately chase it with the pickle brine.

name: Bloody Maria
description: The earthy agave riff on the Bloody Mary, substituting crisp tequila for vodka to pair vegetal pepper notes with seasoned tomato, citrus, and hot sauce.
instructions:
1. Roll (pour back and forth between two shaker tins with ice) tequila, tomato juice, lime juice, lemon juice, Worcestershire sauce, hot sauce, and celery salt.
2. Strain into a tall highball glass filled with ice.
3. Garnish with a leafy celery stalk and a lime wheel.

name: Chrysanthemum
description: An elegant, low-proof Parisian classic built on dry vermouth, sweetened by herbal Bénédictine and perfumed with a whisper of absinthe.
instructions:
1. Combine dry vermouth, Bénédictine, and absinthe in a mixing glass filled with ice.
2. Stir thoroughly for 25-30 seconds until cold and diluted.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe glass.
4. Express orange peel oils over the surface and garnish.
source: Hugo Ensslin, Recipes for Mixed Drinks (1916)

name: Death in the Afternoon
description: Ernest Hemingway's legendary two-ingredient creation pouring potent anise-forward absinthe topped with crisp sparkling wine until milky and opalescent.
instructions:
1. Pour absinthe into a chilled champagne flute or coupe.
2. Slowly top with iced brut sparkling wine or Champagne until it reaches an opalescent milky louche.
3. Serve immediately.

name: Green Ghost
description: A striking 1930s classic pairing London dry gin with the punchy, high-proof herbal intensity of Green Chartreuse, brightened by fresh lime juice.
instructions:
1. Combine gin, Green Chartreuse, and lime juice in a cocktail shaker filled with ice.
2. Shake vigorously for 10-15 seconds until cold.
3. Fine strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Garnish with a lime twist.

name: Norwegian Wood
description: A modern craft masterpiece from PDT in NYC, marrying the caraway and dill spice of aquavit with crisp apple brandy and herbal Yellow Chartreuse.
instructions:
1. Combine aquavit, apple brandy, sweet vermouth, Yellow Chartreuse, and bitters in a mixing glass filled with ice.
2. Stir for 25-30 seconds until well-chilled.
3. Strain into a rocks glass over a large ice cube.
4. Express lemon peel oils over the drink and drop into the glass.

name: Tailspin
description: Robert Hess's nuanced twist on the classic Bijou, swirling gin, sweet vermouth, and Green Chartreuse with an added dash of Campari for bitter depth.
instructions:
1. Combine gin, sweet vermouth, Green Chartreuse, and Campari in a mixing glass with ice.
2. Stir thoroughly for 25-30 seconds until well-chilled.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Express a lemon twist over the glass and garnish with a cocktail cherry.

name: Widow's Kiss
description: A decadent 19th-century jewel built on rich apple brandy, sweetened and perfumed with herbal Yellow Chartreuse and Bénédictine.
instructions:
1. Combine apple brandy, Yellow Chartreuse, Bénédictine, and Angostura bitters in a mixing glass with ice.
2. Stir well for 25-30 seconds until thoroughly chilled.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Drop a cocktail cherry into the bottom of the glass.
source: George J. Kappeler, Modern American Drinks (1895)

name: Final Ward
description: Phil Ward's celebrated modern craft riff on The Last Word, swapping gin and lime for spicy rye whiskey and tart lemon juice.
instructions:
1. Add rye whiskey, Green Chartreuse, maraschino liqueur, and lemon juice to a cocktail shaker with ice.
2. Shake vigorously for 10-15 seconds until well-chilled.
3. Fine strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Garnish with a lemon wheel.

name: Cynar Julep
description: An earthy, bittersweet Italian-American riff on the classic Mint Julep, blending bittersweet Cynar with bourbon, cooling fresh mint, and citrus.
instructions:
1. Gently muddle mint leaves with simple syrup and grapefruit juice in a julep cup.
2. Add Cynar and bourbon, then fill the cup halfway with crushed ice.
3. Swizzle or stir until frost forms on the outside of the cup.
4. Pack with additional crushed ice to create a mounded cone.
5. Garnish lavishly with a fresh mint bouquet and a grapefruit peel.

name: Gunshop Fizz
description: A legendary San Francisco modern craft highball that turns cocktail proportions upside down by pouring two full ounces of aromatic Peychaud's bitters.
instructions:
1. Combine Peychaud's bitters, lemon juice, and simple syrup in a highball glass.
2. Add ice and top with chilled club soda.
3. Gently stir with a barspoon to incorporate.
4. Garnish with a cucumber slice and an orange twist.
source: Kirk Estopinal & Maks Pazuniak, Cure New Orleans (2009)

name: Lemon Drop Shot
description: The quintessential sweet-and-sour party shooter shaking crisp vodka, triple sec, and lemon juice, chased with a bite of a sugar-coated lemon wedge.
instructions:
1. Combine vodka, triple sec, lemon juice, and simple syrup in a cocktail shaker with ice.
2. Shake vigorously until icy cold.
3. Strain into a shot glass.
4. Coat a lemon wedge in granulated sugar on the rim or side, shoot the drink, and bite the wedge.
source: Norman Jay Hobday, Henry Africa's San Francisco (1970s)

name: Mind Eraser
description: A fast-drinking layered 1980s party classic combining vodka and rich coffee liqueur topped with bubbling club soda, taken through a straw in one pull.
instructions:
1. Fill a rocks glass with crushed or cracked ice.
2. Pour coffee liqueur into the base of the glass.
3. Gently float vodka over the back of a barspoon.
4. Top carefully with club soda to keep the distinct dark and clear layers.
5. Serve immediately with a drinking straw.

name: Red Snapper
description: The classic gin-based progenitor of the Bloody Mary, featuring piney London dry gin cut through seasoned tomato juice, lemon, and savory spices.
instructions:
1. Roll (pour back and forth between two shaker tins filled with ice) gin, tomato juice, lemon juice, Worcestershire sauce, hot sauce, and celery salt.
2. Strain into a tall highball glass over fresh ice.
3. Garnish with a leafy celery stalk and a lemon wedge.
source: King Cole Bar, St. Regis Hotel NYC (1930s)

name: French Martini
description: A 1980s New York cocktail renaissance creation pairing crisp vodka with rich black raspberry liqueur and fresh pineapple juice, shaken hard until a creamy, velvety foam crowns the surface.
instructions:
1. Add vodka, black raspberry liqueur, and pineapple juice to a cocktail shaker filled with ice.
2. Shake vigorously for 15 seconds to aerate the pineapple juice and create a dense, silky foam.
3. Fine strain into a chilled coupe or martini glass.
4. Garnish with a fresh raspberry.

name: Sea Breeze
description: The quintessential 1970s highball balancing clean vodka with tart cranberry juice and bitter-bright fresh grapefruit juice over plenty of ice.
instructions:
1. Fill a highball glass with fresh ice cubes.
2. Add vodka, cranberry juice, and grapefruit juice.
3. Stir gently with a barspoon to combine.
4. Garnish with a lime wheel on the rim.

name: Greyhound
description: A refreshingly crisp, minimalist cooler pairing clean vodka with tart, bittersweet grapefruit juice over ice.
instructions:
1. Fill a rocks or highball glass with ice.
2. Pour vodka and grapefruit juice into the glass.
3. Stir briefly to chill and integrate.
4. Garnish with a grapefruit wedge.

name: Salty Dog
description: The salted cousin of the Greyhound, where a coarse salt rim cuts the puckering bitterness of grapefruit juice and enhances the clean spirit.
instructions:
1. Rim a highball or rocks glass with coarse salt.
2. Fill the glass with fresh ice.
3. Add vodka and fresh grapefruit juice.
4. Stir gently to incorporate.
5. Garnish with a grapefruit slice.

name: Godmother
description: The sleek, silky counterpart to the Godfather, blending clean vodka with rich Italian amaretto over a large ice cube for a decadent, nutty sipper.
instructions:
1. Fill a rocks glass with ice.
2. Pour vodka and amaretto into the glass.
3. Stir gently for 15-20 seconds to chill and dilute.
4. Serve neat or on the rocks.

name: Bay Breeze
description: A tropical vacation-leaning highball balancing crisp vodka with tart cranberry juice and sweet, luscious pineapple juice.
instructions:
1. Fill a tall highball glass with ice.
2. Pour vodka, cranberry juice, and pineapple juice into the glass.
3. Stir gently to integrate.
4. Garnish with a lime wheel on the rim.

name: Morning Glory Fizz
description: An iconic 19th-century morning reviver combining blended scotch with lemon, lime, a dash of absinthe, and egg white, shaken frothy and topped with sparkling soda.
instructions:
1. Combine scotch, lemon juice, lime juice, simple syrup, absinthe, and egg white in a shaker without ice.
2. Dry shake vigorously for 15 seconds to whip the egg white.
3. Add ice and shake hard until thoroughly chilled.
4. Strain into a tall highball glass without ice.
5. Top slowly with chilled club soda to push up a towering, velvety foam collar.

name: Mamie Taylor
description: A turn-of-the-century predecessor to the Moscow Mule that pairs blended scotch whisky with fresh lime juice and crisp, bubbly ginger ale.
instructions:
1. Fill a tall highball glass with ice cubes.
2. Add blended scotch and fresh lime juice.
3. Top with chilled ginger ale and stir gently.
4. Garnish with a lime wedge.

name: Cameron's Kick
description: An ingenious cross-border whiskey sour shaking smoky blended scotch with smooth Irish whiskey, bright lemon juice, and nutty almond orgeat.
instructions:
1. Combine blended scotch, Irish whiskey, lemon juice, and orgeat in a cocktail shaker with ice.
2. Shake vigorously for 10-15 seconds until chilled.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Express a lemon peel over the glass and discard.
source: Harry MacElhone, ABC of Mixing Cocktails (1922)

name: Affinity
description: The Scotch Whisky equivalent of the 'Perfect' Manhattan, pairing blended scotch with equal parts sweet and dry vermouth, accented by aromatic and orange bitters.
instructions:
1. Combine blended scotch, sweet vermouth, dry vermouth, and bitters in a mixing glass with ice.
2. Stir for 25-30 seconds until well-chilled and integrated.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Express lemon peel oils over the drink and garnish with a cherry.

name: Artist's Special
description: A 1920s Parisian jazz-age classic blending blended scotch with nutty dry sherry, tart lemon juice, and fruity pomegranate grenadine.
instructions:
1. Combine blended scotch, dry sherry, lemon juice, and grenadine in a cocktail shaker filled with ice.
2. Shake hard for 10-15 seconds until well-chilled.
3. Fine strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Express lemon peel oils over the drink and drop the twist into the glass.
source: Harry MacElhone, Harry's New York Bar, Paris (c. 1920s)

name: Chancellor
description: A rich, sophisticated variation on the Rob Roy, marrying blended scotch with ruby port wine and dry vermouth for deep vinous warmth.
instructions:
1. Add blended scotch, port, dry vermouth, and Angostura bitters to a mixing glass filled with ice.
2. Stir thoroughly for 25-30 seconds until cold and diluted.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Express an orange twist over the surface and drop it into the glass.

name: Corpse Reviver No. 1
description: The older, vinous progenitor to the famous No. 2, stirring rich cognac, crisp apple brandy, and sweet vermouth into an elegant, comforting digestif.
instructions:
1. Combine cognac, apple brandy, and sweet vermouth in a mixing glass with ice.
2. Stir for 25-30 seconds until well-chilled.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe glass.
4. Garnish with an expressed orange twist.

name: East India Cocktail
description: A lavish 19th-century brandy classic blending rich cognac with orange curaçao, pineapple juice, and a delicate touch of maraschino liqueur.
instructions:
1. Combine cognac, orange curaçao, pineapple juice, maraschino liqueur, and Angostura bitters in a mixing glass with ice.
2. Stir well for 25-30 seconds until icy cold.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Drop a brandied cocktail cherry into the glass.
source: Harry Johnson, New and Improved Bartender's Manual (1882)

name: Porto Flip
description: The definitive Victorian tavern flip combining rich cognac and ruby port with a whole egg, shaken vigorously into a decadent, custard-smooth dessert cocktail.
instructions:
1. Combine cognac, ruby port, simple syrup, and the whole egg in a cocktail shaker.
2. Dry shake vigorously without ice for 15 seconds to emulsify the egg.
3. Add ice cubes and shake hard for another 15 seconds until frosty and rich.
4. Strain into a chilled coupe or sour glass.
5. Dust generously with freshly grated nutmeg.
source: Jerry Thomas, How to Mix Drinks (1862)

name: Harvard
description: An Ivy League classic from the 1890s Manhattan cocktail tradition, swapping whiskey for rich cognac, stirred with sweet vermouth and topped with a splash of effervescent club soda.
instructions:
1. Combine cognac, sweet vermouth, and Angostura bitters in a mixing glass with ice.
2. Stir for 25-30 seconds until well-chilled.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Top with a splash of chilled club soda and express orange peel oils over the surface.
source: George J. Kappeler, Modern American Drinks (1895)

name: Brandy Daisy
description: A vibrant Victorian sour pairing rich French cognac with tart lemon juice, herbal Yellow Chartreuse, and a lively spritz of club soda.
instructions:
1. Add cognac, Yellow Chartreuse, lemon juice, and simple syrup to a cocktail shaker with ice.
2. Shake vigorously for 10-15 seconds until well-chilled.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe or goblet over crushed ice.
4. Top with chilled club soda and garnish with a lemon wheel and mint sprig.

name: Star Cocktail
description: A turn-of-the-century Manhattan variation swapping whiskey for crisp apple brandy, stirred with sweet vermouth and aromatic bitters.
instructions:
1. Combine apple brandy, sweet vermouth, and Angostura bitters in a mixing glass with ice.
2. Stir for 25-30 seconds until well-chilled.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Express lemon peel oils over the surface and drop the twist into the glass.
source: George J. Kappeler, Modern American Drinks (1895)

name: Batanga
description: Don Javier Delgado Corona's legendary Mexican tavern staple combining 100% agave tequila, fresh lime juice, and Mexican cola in a salt-rimmed glass, stirred with a wooden-handled knife.
instructions:
1. Rim a tall highball glass with coarse salt.
2. Fill the glass with ice cubes.
3. Add blanco tequila and fresh lime juice.
4. Top with chilled cola.
5. Stir thoroughly with a knife and garnish with a lime wedge.
source: Don Javier Delgado Corona, La Capilla Bar, Tequila, Mexico (1961)

name: Cantarito
description: The beloved Jalisco street-stand cooler combining blanco tequila with a trio of fresh citrus juices, topped with fizzy grapefruit soda in a salt-rimmed clay jar or tall glass.
instructions:
1. Rim a highball glass or clay cantarito cup with coarse salt.
2. Fill the glass with ice cubes.
3. Add blanco tequila, fresh grapefruit juice, orange juice, and lime juice.
4. Top with grapefruit soda and stir gently to combine.
5. Garnish with a fresh grapefruit wedge.

name: Tequila Sunrise
description: The vibrant 1970s rock 'n' roll staple layering blanco tequila and orange juice with a slow sink of rich grenadine to create a stunning sunset gradient.
instructions:
1. Fill a tall highball glass with ice.
2. Add blanco tequila and fresh orange juice.
3. Stir gently to integrate.
4. Slowly pour grenadine down the inside edge of the glass so it sinks to the bottom.
5. Garnish with an orange wheel and a cocktail cherry on a skewer without stirring.
source: Bobby Lozoff & Billy Rice, Trident Restaurant, Sausalito (1970s)

name: Matador
description: A breezy mid-century Mexican classic shaking crisp blanco tequila with sweet pineapple juice and tart fresh lime juice.
instructions:
1. Combine blanco tequila, pineapple juice, and lime juice in a cocktail shaker filled with ice.
2. Shake hard for 10-15 seconds until cold and foamy.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe glass.
4. Garnish with a lime wheel.

name: Picador
description: The historical 1937 London predecessor to the modern Margarita, shaking blanco tequila with orange triple sec and tart lime juice in crisp harmony.
instructions:
1. Combine tequila, triple sec, and fresh lime juice in a cocktail shaker filled with ice.
2. Shake vigorously for 10-15 seconds until frosty.
3. Fine strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Garnish with a lime wheel.

name: Mexican Mule
description: The agave-fueled riff on the Moscow Mule (also known as El Burro), matching peppery blanco tequila with fresh lime juice and spicy ginger beer.
instructions:
1. Fill a highball glass or copper mug with ice.
2. Add blanco tequila and fresh lime juice.
3. Top with spicy chilled ginger beer.
4. Stir gently to integrate.
5. Garnish with a lime wheel and a fresh sprig of mint.

name: Brave Bull
description: A dark, potent two-ingredient Mexican cousin to the Black Russian, pairing robust 100% agave tequila with rich, sweet coffee liqueur over ice.
instructions:
1. Fill an old fashioned or rocks glass with ice.
2. Add blanco tequila and coffee liqueur.
3. Stir gently for 20 seconds until well-chilled.
4. Express a lemon twist over the surface and drop it into the glass.

name: Vodka Martini
description: The pristine mid-century iteration of the Martini, matching crisp vodka with dry vermouth and a dash of orange bitters for a clean, silky aperitif.
instructions:
1. Combine vodka, dry vermouth, and orange bitters in a mixing glass filled with ice.
2. Stir thoroughly for 25-30 seconds until ice cold and properly diluted.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe or martini glass.
4. Express lemon peel oils over the drink and drop the twist in, or garnish with an olive.
source: David Embury, The Fine Art of Mixing Drinks (1948)

name: Lemon Drop
description: San Francisco's iconic 1970s fern bar cocktail, shaking crisp vodka with orange triple sec, fresh lemon juice, and simple syrup in a sugar-rimmed coupe.
instructions:
1. Rim half of a chilled coupe glass with a lemon wedge and dip into superfine sugar.
2. Add vodka, triple sec, lemon juice, and simple syrup to a shaker filled with ice.
3. Shake hard for 10-15 seconds until frosty and cold.
4. Fine strain into the prepared coupe.
5. Float a thin lemon wheel on the surface.
source: Norman Jay Hobday, Henry Africa's San Francisco (1970s)

name: Vodka Gimlet
description: The sleek modern variation on the classic Gimlet, substituting neutral vodka to allow the bright, tart punch of fresh lime juice and sweetness to shine.
instructions:
1. Add vodka, fresh lime juice, and simple syrup to a cocktail shaker filled with ice.
2. Shake hard for 10-15 seconds until thoroughly chilled.
3. Fine strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Garnish with a fresh lime wheel.

name: Vodka Collins
description: A light, sparkling mid-century cooler shaking vodka with fresh lemon juice and simple syrup, topped with effervescent club soda in a tall glass.
instructions:
1. Add vodka, lemon juice, and simple syrup to a cocktail shaker with ice.
2. Shake briefly for 5-10 seconds to chill.
3. Strain into a tall highball or collins glass filled with fresh ice cubes.
4. Top with chilled club soda and stir gently.
5. Garnish with a lemon wheel and a cocktail cherry.

name: Screwdriver
description: An American mid-century staple pairing clean vodka with freshly squeezed orange juice over plenty of ice in an effortless two-ingredient cooler.
instructions:
1. Fill a highball or rocks glass with ice.
2. Pour vodka over the ice.
3. Top with chilled orange juice.
4. Stir gently with a barspoon to combine.
5. Garnish with a fresh orange slice.
source: American Oil Workers, Persian Gulf / Time Magazine (1949)

name: Cape Codder
description: The foundational vodka and cranberry highball named for Massachusetts' cranberry country, brightened with a fresh squeeze of lime.
instructions:
1. Fill a highball glass with fresh ice cubes.
2. Add vodka and fresh lime juice.
3. Top with chilled cranberry juice.
4. Stir gently to combine.
5. Garnish with a lime wedge on the rim.

name: Madras
description: A bright, vibrant 1980s beach-bar favorite that pairs clean vodka with tart cranberry juice and sweet orange juice over ice.
instructions:
1. Fill a tall highball glass with ice.
2. Pour in vodka and cranberry juice.
3. Top with fresh orange juice.
4. Stir gently to integrate.
5. Garnish with a lime wheel.

name: Woo Woo
description: A spirited 1980s disco-era party cocktail matching vodka with sweet peach schnapps and tart cranberry juice over cracked ice.
instructions:
1. Fill a highball glass with ice.
2. Add vodka and peach schnapps.
3. Top with tart cranberry juice.
4. Stir gently to incorporate.
5. Garnish with a lime wedge.
source: First Edition Bar, Bayside Queens NYC (c. 1980s)

name: Gypsy Queen
description: A sophisticated pre-war classic from Manhattan's Russian Tea Room, stirring smooth vodka with rich herbal Bénédictine and aromatic bitters.
instructions:
1. Combine vodka, Bénédictine, and Angostura bitters in a mixing glass filled with ice.
2. Stir thoroughly for 25-30 seconds until cold and diluted.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Express lemon peel oils over the drink and drop the twist into the glass.

name: Vodka Sour
description: A velvety, elegant classic sour blending clean vodka with freshly squeezed lemon juice, simple syrup, and egg white, shaken into a thick creamy froth.
instructions:
1. Combine vodka, lemon juice, simple syrup, and egg white in a cocktail shaker.
2. Dry shake vigorously without ice for 15 seconds to whip the egg white into foam.
3. Add ice cubes and shake hard for another 10-15 seconds until frosty cold.
4. Double strain into a chilled coupe glass.
5. Dot the foam with a few drops of Angostura bitters and garnish with a lemon wheel.

name: Long Island Iced Tea
description: The notoriously potent highball that deceptively tastes like sweet iced tea by shaking five clear spirits with lemon and topping with a splash of cola.
instructions:
1. Add vodka, gin, light rum, tequila, triple sec, lemon juice, and simple syrup to a cocktail shaker with ice.
2. Shake briefly for 5-10 seconds to chill and combine.
3. Strain into a tall highball glass filled with fresh ice.
4. Top with a splash of chilled cola for color.
5. Garnish with a lemon wheel.
source: Robert 'Rosebud' Butt, Oak Beach Inn, Long Island (1972)

name: Cuba Libre
description: The historic Havana highball elevated beyond a simple rum and cola by muddling fresh lime directly into the glass with light rum, ice, and bubbly cola.
instructions:
1. Squeeze fresh lime juice into a highball glass and drop in the spent lime wedge.
2. Fill the glass with fresh ice cubes.
3. Add light rum and top with chilled cola.
4. Stir gently with a barspoon to combine.

name: Mimosa
description: The undisputed queen of brunch cocktails, marrying crisp sparkling wine with freshly squeezed orange juice in bubbly, golden harmony.
instructions:
1. Pour chilled fresh orange juice into a champagne flute.
2. Gently top with chilled sparkling wine or Champagne to maintain carbonation.
3. Stir once with a barspoon if needed.
4. Garnish with an orange peel twist.

name: Champagne Cocktail
description: A sparkling Victorian classic where aromatic bitters and rich cognac elevate brut champagne into a dancing pillar of aromatic bubbles.
instructions:
1. Add simple syrup, cognac, and Angostura bitters to the base of a chilled champagne flute.
2. Slowly top with cold brut sparkling wine or Champagne.
3. Express lemon peel oils over the glass and garnish.
source: Jerry Thomas, How to Mix Drinks (1862)

name: Kir Royale
description: A festive French bistro classic dressing dry sparkling wine with a ruby measure of sweet blackcurrant Crème de Cassis.
instructions:
1. Pour crème de cassis into the bottom of a chilled champagne flute.
2. Gently top with cold dry sparkling wine or Champagne.
3. Garnish with a fresh raspberry or blackberry.

name: Kir
description: The traditional Burgundian café aperitif combining crisp dry white wine with a measure of sweet, dark Crème de Cassis.
instructions:
1. Add crème de cassis to a chilled white wine glass.
2. Top with cold dry white wine.
3. Stir gently to integrate into a luminous ruby-red aperitif.

name: Black Velvet
description: A regal 1861 London institution pouring equal parts roasted, creamy dry Irish stout and crisp, effervescent sparkling wine.
instructions:
1. Fill a champagne flute or glass halfway with chilled dry stout.
2. Slowly pour cold sparkling wine or Champagne over the back of a spoon to float over the dark stout, or gently stir together.

name: Amaretto Sour
description: Jeffrey Morgenthaler's benchmark craft cocktail recipe, bolstering sweet Italian amaretto with cask-strength bourbon, fresh lemon, and silky egg white.
instructions:
1. Combine amaretto, bourbon, lemon juice, simple syrup, and egg white in a shaker.
2. Dry shake without ice for 15 seconds to whip the egg white.
3. Add ice cubes and shake hard for another 15 seconds until frosty and cold.
4. Strain over fresh ice in a rocks glass.
5. Garnish with a lemon wheel and a brandied cherry.

name: John Collins
description: The American whiskey sister of the Tom Collins, shaking bourbon with fresh lemon and sugar before topping with bubbling club soda.
instructions:
1. Combine bourbon, lemon juice, and simple syrup in a cocktail shaker with ice.
2. Shake briefly for 5-10 seconds to chill.
3. Strain into a tall highball glass filled with ice.
4. Top with chilled club soda and stir gently.
5. Garnish with a lemon wheel and a cocktail cherry.
source: Jerry Thomas, How to Mix Drinks (1876)

name: Ward Eight
description: Boston's historic 1898 celebration sour shaking spicy rye whiskey with tart lemon juice, fresh orange juice, and rich pomegranate grenadine.
instructions:
1. Combine rye whiskey, lemon juice, orange juice, and grenadine in a shaker filled with ice.
2. Shake vigorously for 10-15 seconds until thoroughly chilled.
3. Fine strain into a chilled coupe glass.
4. Garnish with a cocktail cherry.

name: Horse's Neck
description: A dashing 19th-century American highball pairing bourbon and ginger ale with aromatic bitters, framed by a continuous dramatic lemon peel spiral.
instructions:
1. Cut a long, unbroken spiral peel from an entire lemon and drape it inside a tall highball glass, curling around the inside rim and base.
2. Fill the glass with ice cubes to hold the peel in place.
3. Add bourbon and bitters, then top with ginger ale.
4. Stir gently to integrate.

name: Gin Sour
description: The foundational botanical sour balancing crisp London dry gin with freshly squeezed lemon juice, simple syrup, and a velvety head of whipped egg white.
instructions:
1. Combine gin, lemon juice, simple syrup, and egg white in a cocktail shaker.
2. Dry shake without ice for 15 seconds to whip the egg white.
3. Add ice cubes and shake hard for another 10-15 seconds until icy cold.
4. Fine strain into a chilled coupe.
5. Garnish with a lemon wheel and a cherry.
source: Jerry Thomas, How to Mix Drinks (1862)

name: Derby
description: A bright, citrusy mid-century classic pairing rich Kentucky bourbon with sweet vermouth, orange curaçao, and tart lime juice.
instructions:
1. Combine bourbon, sweet vermouth, orange curaçao, and fresh lime juice in a cocktail shaker filled with ice.
2. Shake vigorously for 10-15 seconds until well-chilled.
3. Fine strain into a chilled coupe glass.
4. Garnish with a fresh mint leaf and a lime wheel.
